emperors.bio_md:
# 晋废帝 · 主要事迹

司马奕字延龄，成帝子，哀帝弟，封东海王。兴宁三年哀帝崩，奕即位，改元太和。废帝在位六年，无大失德；然其时桓温北伐前燕，太和四年至枋头，粮尽退军，大败而归——北伐之望绝，桓温之威受挫。

桓温素有异志，枋头之败后，名实俱损，遂思借废立以立威：太和六年十一月，温入朝，诬帝「痿疾不能男」，以太后令废帝为东海王，又降为海西公。帝被废后，温犹使人构陷，帝「深自晦匿」，杜口不谈朝事，惟以声色自晦——「海西公」遂得善终。

太元十一年，海西公薨于吴，年四十五。史家论废帝：「帝实无大过，温欲立威而废之。」东晋门阀政治，权臣可以一言废立天子，自桓温废帝始；其后桓玄篡位、刘裕禅代，皆沿此轨。废帝以一庸主之身，遭权臣之诬，虽保首领，然中国皇权之尊严，自此扫地。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷008《海西公纪》、卷098《桓温传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Yi, styled Yanling, was a son of Emperor Cheng and younger brother of Emperor Ai, enfeoffed Prince of Donghai. On Ai's death in the 3rd year of Xingning he took the throne, changing the era to Taihe. Six years he reigned without great fault; but in the 4th year of Taihe Huan Wen's northern expedition against Former Yan ran out of grain at Fangtou and came back in ruin — the hope of the north was gone, and Wen's prestige was wounded.

Wen, who harbored designs, sought to restore his name by deposing the emperor: in the eleventh month of the 6th year of Taihe he came to court, falsely charged the emperor with impotence — "the emperor cannot father sons" — and by the empress dowager's edict deposed him as Prince of Donghai, later reducing him to Duke of Haixi. Even in exile Wen's men came to slander him; the deposed emperor "hid himself utterly," never speaking of court affairs, hiding in music and women — and so the Duke of Haixi died in his bed.

In the 11th year of Taiyuan the Duke of Haixi died in Wu at forty-five. The historians say: "The emperor was in fact without great fault; Wen deposed him to awe the court." That a strong minister could depose an emperor on a word began with Huan Wen's act; Huan Xuan's usurpation and Liu Yu's abdication followed the same road. A mediocre sovereign done to death by calumny, he kept his life but not his throne — and the dignity of the imperial office, in Eastern Jin, was never quite the same.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 8 ("Benji of the Duke of Haixi"), ch. 98 (biography of Huan Wen) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 晋简文帝 · 主要事迹

司马昱字道万，元帝少子，封会稽王。性清虚寡欲，尤善玄言，为东晋清谈宗主；历成、康、穆、哀、废五朝，长期辅政，录尚书事。太和六年，桓温废帝，迎立昱即位，改元咸安——时昱年五十二，在帝位不及一年。

简文帝之立，纯为桓温废立之需：温入朝，昱垂涕而受禅，即位后，温欲求九锡、觊觎禅让。帝与王坦之、谢安等周旋，温病笃而请不行——「温求九锡未成」，晋祚得延。咸安二年七月，帝崩于东堂，年五十三，遗诏「大司马温依周公居摄故事」，孝武帝曜即位，时年十一。

史臣评简文帝：「清虚寡欲，尤善玄言。」以清谈名士坐天子位，本无治世之才，亦无争权之志；其在位之业，惟在婉拒桓温之禅让，为司马氏延祚十载。然谢安、王坦之能周旋其间，实赖其主之谦抑——简文一朝，虽无德政，然以「受制权臣而无尺寸之权」之身，得全晋祚，亦不失为乱世自全之道。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷009《简文帝纪》、卷098《桓温传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Yu, styled Daowan, was the youngest son of Emperor Yuan, enfeoffed Prince of Kuajji. Pure and passionless by nature, a master of metaphysical talk, he was the patriarch of Eastern Jin's pure conversation; through the reigns of Cheng, Kang, Mu, Ai, and the deposed emperor he served as regent and grand secretary. In the 6th year of Taihe Huan Wen deposed the emperor and brought in Yu, changing the era to Xian'an — Yu was fifty-two, and reigned under a year.

His accession was wholly Huan Wen's doing: Wen came to court, and Yu, weeping, accepted the throne. Then Wen sought the nine gifts and looked toward abdication. The emperor, with Wang Tanzhi and Xie An, played for time; Wen fell ill, and the petition failed — "Wen's bid for the nine gifts came to nothing," and the Jin line was prolonged. In the seventh month of the 2nd year of Xian'an he died in the eastern hall at fifty-three, his will charging "the grand marshal Wen, after the manner of the Duke of Zhou's regency"; Emperor Xiaowu, eleven years old, succeeded.

The historians say of him: "Pure and passionless, a master of metaphysical talk." A conversationalist set on the imperial throne, he had neither the talent nor the will to rule; his single achievement was parrying Huan Wen's abdication, buying the Jin house a decade. That Xie An and Wang Tanzhi could play their game was thanks to their sovereign's humility. His reign had no great deeds; but by enduring the strong minister's grip without an inch of power, he kept the altars standing — no mean art in that age.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 9 ("Benji of Emperor Jianwen"), ch. 98 (biography of Huan Wen) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 晋孝武帝 · 主要事迹

司马曜字昌明，简文帝子，母李氏。咸安二年简文帝崩，曜即位，年十一，褚太后曾临朝，谢安等执政。宁康元年桓温卒，禅代之威胁消，东晋始有振作之机。太元元年，帝亲政。

孝武之朝，以淝水之战为标志：太元八年，前秦苻坚倾国南下，号称百万，谢石、谢玄率北府兵八万拒之。淝水一战，秦军大溃，草木皆兵、风声鹤唳，苻坚狼狈北遁——东晋转危为安，南朝百年偏安之局自此定。战后乘胜北伐，收复河南诸城，然得而复失。太元十年谢安卒，帝用其弟司马道子执政，政道渐衰。

亲政之后，孝武帝渐耽于酒色，日与道子酣饮，国政弛废；太元二十一年，帝醉后与张贵人戏言，贵人大惧，使婢以被蒙帝首，弑于清暑殿——在位二十四年，一代中兴之主，竟以戏言死于妇人手，年三十五。

史家评孝武帝：「初赖谢安，淝水一战保江南；后溺于酒色，委政道子。」淝水之战为东晋中兴之顶点，亦为其衰亡之转折：战后司马道子与桓氏相争，孙恩、卢循之乱继起，刘裕以寒门起于京口——东晋之亡，已见端于孝武之世。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷009《孝武帝纪》、卷079《谢玄传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Yao, styled Changming, was the son of Emperor Jianwen by Lady Li. On Jianwen's death in the 2nd year of Xian'an he took the throne at eleven; Empress Chu held court for a time, and Xie An governed. In the 1st year of Ningkang Huan Wen died, the menace of abdication was gone, and Eastern Jin had its chance. In the 1st year of Taiyuan the emperor took the government in person.

His reign is defined by the Battle of the Fei River: in the 8th year of Taiyuan Fu Jian of Former Qin came south in overwhelming force, "a million men," and Xie Shi and Xie Xuan met him with eighty thousand of the Northern Garrison. At the Fei River the Qin army collapsed — "every grass and tree a soldier, the wind and cranes the enemy's cries" — and Fu Jian fled north in rout. Eastern Jin was saved, and the century of the southern dynasties was set. Pressing north on the victory, the Jin armies took the cities of Henan — won and lost again. In the 10th year of Taiyuan Xie An died, and the emperor turned to his brother Sima Daozi; the way of government decayed.

In person rule he sank into wine and women, drinking daily with Daozi while the government went slack; in the 21st year of Taiyuan, drunk, he mocked Lady Zhang, who in terror had her maids smother him in the Qingshu Hall — twenty-four years a sovereign, and a middling restorer killed by a jest at a woman's hands, aged thirty-five.

The historians say: "Relying on Xie An at first, the Fei River battle saved the south; later he drowned in wine and women, and left government to Daozi." The Fei River was the summit of Eastern Jin's recovery and the hinge of its decline: after it, Daozi and the Huans contended, Sun En and Lu Xun rose, and Liu Yu, a common soldier, rose from Jingkou — the fall of Eastern Jin was already in view in Xiaowu's reign.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 9 ("Benji of Emperor Xiaowu"), ch. 79 (biography of Xie Xuan) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.summary: 不慧，寒暑不辨，在位二十二年而政归权臣：孙恩乱、桓玄篡、刘裕起兵反正，义熙年间裕灭南燕后秦；义熙十四年为刘裕使人缢杀。
emperors.summary_en: Dull of mind, unable to tell heat from cold, he reigned twenty-two years while strong ministers ruled: Sun En's revolt, Huan Xuan's usurpation, Liu Yu's rising and restoration — in the Yixi years Yu destroyed Southern Yan and Later Qin, and in the 14th year of Yixi he had the emperor strangled.

timeline.summary: 孝武帝长子，不慧。

timeline.summary_en: Sun En rose against Kuajji, and the south was thrown into turmoil.

timeline.summary_en: Huan Xuan broke Sima Yuanxian, entered Jiankang, and took the titles of grand commandant over all offices.

timeline.summary: 桓玄废帝为平固王，建国号楚。
timeline.summary_en: Huan Xuan degraded the emperor to Prince of Pinggu and founded his own realm of Chu.

timeline.title: 刘裕起兵
timeline.summary: 刘裕等起兵京口，玄败死，帝反正。
timeline.summary_en: Liu Yu and the others rose at Jingkou; Xuan was routed and killed, and the emperor was restored.

timeline.title: 改元义熙
timeline.summary: 反正后改元义熙。
timeline.summary_en: After the restoration the era was changed to Yixi.

timeline.title: 裕灭南燕
timeline.summary: 刘裕克广固，斩慕容超，灭南燕。
timeline.summary_en: Liu Yu took Guanggu, beheaded Murong Chao, and destroyed Southern Yan.

timeline.title: 卢循逼建康
timeline.summary: 卢循、徐道覆攻建康，刘裕回师击破之。
timeline.summary_en: Lu Xun and Xu Daofu attacked Jiankang; Liu Yu hurried back and broke them.

timeline.title: 裕北伐后秦
timeline.title_en: Liu Yu's Campaign against Later Qin
timeline.summary: 刘裕北伐后秦，入洛阳，明年克长安。
timeline.summary_en: Liu Yu campaigned against Later Qin, entered Luoyang, and took Chang'an the next year.

timeline.title: 安帝被弑
timeline.summary: 刘裕使人缢帝于东堂，立恭帝德文。
timeline.summary_en: Liu Yu had the emperor strangled in the eastern hall and set up his brother Dewen as Emperor Gong.

timeline.title: 安帝总评
timeline.summary: 帝不惠，至于寒暑不辨，权归台辅，坐致桓玄之篡、刘裕之兴。
timeline.summary_en: Unfortunate and unable to tell heat from cold, he left all power to the ministers and sat by while Huan Xuan usurped and Liu Yu rose.

emperors.bio_md:
# 晋安帝 · 主要事迹

司马德宗，孝武帝长子，母陈氏。安帝「不慧，自少及长，口不能言，虽寒暑饥饱亦不能辨」，为东晋最愚之主。太元二十一年孝武帝被弑，德宗即位，年十五，司马道子、元显父子执政。

安帝在位二十二年，东晋政局天翻地覆：隆安三年孙恩起兵攻会稽，江南大乱；元兴元年桓玄入京，杀元显；元兴二年，桓玄废帝为平固王，建号楚国——东晋第一次亡于权臣之手。元兴三年，刘裕起兵京口，讨平桓玄，帝反正，改元义熙。义熙五年刘裕灭南燕，克广固，斩慕容超；义熙六年破卢循；义熙十二至十三年，裕北伐后秦，克洛阳、长安——东晋武功，至此极盛，然皆刘裕之功，非安帝之业。

义熙十四年，刘裕急于禅代，使人缢帝于东堂，立其弟德文（恭帝）。安帝以痴愚之身坐帝位二十二年，目睹桓玄之篡、刘裕之兴，而始终懵然无知——东晋之兴衰，皆与其人无关。史家论曰：「帝不惠，权归台辅。」以如此之主延续晋祚二十余年，实赖权臣相争之局；刘裕一旦决意，晋祚遂移。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷010《安帝纪》、卷099《桓玄传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Dezong, eldest son of Emperor Xiaowu by Lady Chen, was "unfortunate — from childhood to manhood he could not speak, and could not tell heat from cold or hunger from fullness," the dullest of the Eastern Jin sovereigns. In the 21st year of Taiyuan, Emperor Xiaowu slain, Dezong took the throne at fifteen, with Sima Daozi and his son Yuanxian governing.

Twenty-two years he sat while the dynasty was turned upside down: in the 3rd year of Long'an Sun En rose against Kuajji and the south was in turmoil; in the 1st year of Yuanxing Huan Xuan entered the capital and slew Yuanxian; in the 2nd year of Yuanxing Xuan degraded the emperor to Prince of Pinggu and founded his realm of Chu — the first fall of Eastern Jin to a usurper. In the 3rd year of Yuanxing Liu Yu rose at Jingkou, destroyed Xuan, and restored the emperor; the era was changed to Yixi. In the 5th year of Yixi Yu destroyed Southern Yan, took Guanggu, and beheaded Murong Chao; in the 6th he broke Lu Xun; from the 12th to the 13th he campaigned against Later Qin, entering Luoyang and taking Chang'an — the greatest military glory of Eastern Jin, and all of it Liu Yu's, none of it the emperor's.

In the 14th year of Yixi, in haste for the abdication, Liu Yu had the emperor strangled in the eastern hall and set up his brother Dewen as Emperor Gong. A mindless man on the throne for twenty-two years, Dezong watched Huan Xuan's usurpation and Liu Yu's rise without ever knowing them — Eastern Jin's rise and fall passed him by. The historians say: "Unfortunate, he left all power to the ministers." That such a sovereign prolonged the Jin line twenty years was the accident of the strong ministers' rivalry; the moment Liu Yu made up his mind, the mandate passed.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 10 ("Benji of Emperor An"), ch. 99 (biography of Huan Xuan) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 晋恭帝 · 主要事迹

司马德文，安帝弟，封琅邪王。义熙十四年，刘裕使人缢杀安帝，迎立德文即位，改元元熙。恭帝即位时年三十三，深知刘裕之志：元熙元年，裕进爵宋王，加九锡，禅代之势已成。

元熙二年六月，刘裕使人讽帝禅位，恭帝自知不免，遂书赤纸为诏，逊位于宋——东晋自元帝南渡，传十一帝一百零四年而亡。帝逊位后，封为零陵王，居秣陵，敕令其家勿与刘氏通婚，深自韬晦；然永初二年九月，刘裕遣人授帝毒酒，帝以「佛教自杀者不得复人身」辞，使者遂以被掩杀之，年三十六。

晋祚之亡，与汉、魏之亡相类，皆以禅让为名：然汉禅于魏，魏禅于晋，晋又禅于宋，禅让之局，愈演愈露其伪。恭帝逊位一年而遭杀害，较之汉献帝之善终、魏元帝之全生，尤为可哀。史家论晋之亡：非亡于恭帝，而亡于门阀政治之积弊——刘裕以寒门武人取司马氏之天下，六朝门阀之局，自此而变。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷010《恭帝纪》、宋书卷001《武帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Dewen, younger brother of Emperor An, was enfeoffed Prince of Langya. In the 14th year of Yixi, after Liu Yu had Emperor An strangled, Dewen was brought to the throne, changing the era to Yuanxi. He was thirty-three and knew Liu Yu's mind: in the 1st year of Yuanxi Yu was made King of Song with the nine gifts complete — the abdication was prepared.

In the sixth month of the 2nd year of Yuanxi, Liu Yu had men hint at abdication; Emperor Gong, seeing no escape, wrote the abdication edict himself and yielded to Song — Eastern Jin, eleven sovereigns and one hundred and four years from Yuan's crossing south, was no more. The former emperor was enfeoffed Duke of Lingling and settled at Moling, ordered his household to avoid marriage with the Liu house, and hid himself utterly; but in the ninth month of the 2nd year of Yongchu Liu Yu sent men with poisoned wine. "The Buddhists say one who dies by his own hand cannot be reborn a man," said the emperor, refusing; the messengers smothered him with a blanket. He was thirty-six.

The fall of Jin, like the fall of Han and Wei, wore the name of abdication — but the sequence of Han yielding to Wei, Wei to Jin, and Jin to Song showed the mask wearing thin. Gong was murdered a year after his abdication, unlike Emperor Xian of Han, who ended his days in peace, or Emperor Yuan of Wei, who was spared. The historians say Jin fell not to Gong but to the accumulated disease of aristocratic politics; and in Liu Yu, a common soldier, taking the Sima realm, the age of the great clans began its turn.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 10 ("Benji of Emperor Gong"), and the *Songshu*, ch. 1 ("Benji of Emperor Wu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 宋武帝 · 主要事迹

刘裕字德舆，小字寄奴，彭城人，侨居京口。出身寒微，「布衣起家，实由武功」：初为北府兵将，元兴三年与刘毅、何无忌等起兵京口，讨平桓玄，迎晋安帝复辟——「再造晋室」之功，实自裕始。

义熙年间，刘裕总揽朝政，武功极盛：义熙五年北伐南燕，克广固、斩慕容超；义熙六年回师破卢循、徐道覆，保建康；义熙十二年北伐后秦，次年入长安，姚泓出降——五胡以来沦陷的中原，一度光复。然留子义真镇关中，旋为赫连勃勃所夺，「得而复失」。义熙土断、抑制豪强，为南朝集权张本。

永初元年，晋恭帝禅位，刘裕即皇帝位，国号宋，改元永初——晋亡宋立，南朝自此始。永初三年，裕崩于西殿，年六十。史称裕「奇才远略，功百晋宣」；然性猜忌，「功臣多不终」，杀刘毅、诸葛长民等。刘裕以寒门之身取天下，终结门阀政治之垄断，南朝以降，「王与马共天下」之局遂变为「寒人掌机要」——其开国规模，实为南朝之最。

> 本地参考：点校本《宋书》卷001《武帝纪》、卷002《武帝纪中》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Yu, styled Deyu, childhood name Jinu, was a man of Pengcheng settled at Jingkou. Of common birth, "he rose from the cloth and took the realm by arms": a general of the Northern Garrison, in the 3rd year of Yuanxing he rose at Jingkou with Liu Yi and He Wuji, destroyed Huan Xuan, and restored Emperor An — the "re-founding of the Jin house" was his work.

In the Yixi years, holding the government, he reached the height of arms: in the 5th year he destroyed Southern Yan, taking Guanggu and beheading Murong Chao; in the 6th he hurried back to break Lu Xun and Xu Daofu and save Jiankang; in the 12th he campaigned against Later Qin, entering Chang'an the next year as Yao Hong surrendered — the Central Plains, lost to the barbarians, were recovered for a moment. But his son Yizhen, left to hold Guanzhong, was soon driven out by Helian Bobo: "won and lost again." His registration of the displaced and his checking of the powerful prepared the centralization of the southern courts.

In the 1st year of Yongchu Emperor Gong of Jin abdicated; Yu took the throne, styled the realm Song, and changed the era — Jin fell, Song rose, and the Southern Dynasties began. He died in the western hall in the 3rd year of Yongchu at sixty. The histories call him "a rare genius of far-seeing strategy, his merit a hundred times Sima Yi's"; but he was jealous, and "few of his meritorious ministers came to a good end" — Liu Yi, Zhuge Changmin, and the rest were slain. A common man who took the realm, he broke the great clans' monopoly; the age of "Wang and Sima sharing the realm" gave way to the ascendancy of the humble — his founding measures were the greatest of the Southern Dynasties.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Songshu*, ch. 1 and 2 ("Benji of Emperor Wu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 宋少帝 · 主要事迹

刘义符字车兵，武帝长子。永初三年武帝崩，义符即位，年十七，改元景平。徐羡之、傅亮、谢晦、檀道济等受遗辅政。少帝「游戏无度，不亲政事」，史载其在后宫与宫人游戏，又于华林园列肆酤酒，亲自为估——少年天子，毫无君主之仪。

景平元年，北魏南攻，司、兖、豫诸郡多陷魏，边事紧急；少帝不以为意，军政尽委权臣。景平二年五月，徐羡之等以太后令废帝为营阳王，幽于吴郡，旋使人弑之，年十九。废立之际，刘裕诸子尚幼，权臣迎立宜都王刘义隆，即宋文帝。

少帝之废，开南朝「权臣废立」之先例：此后南朝三百余年，废君弑主之事不绝，萧道成之弑后废帝、萧鸾之废郁林海陵，皆沿此轨。少帝以游戏而失国，固其自取；然「主少国疑、权臣擅命」之局，实自刘宋肇始——宋武之猜忌与少帝之轻浮，共同铸成南朝政治的底色。

> 本地参考：点校本《宋书》卷004《少帝纪》、卷043《徐羡之传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

Liu Yifu, styled Chebing, was the eldest son of Emperor Wu. On his father's death in the 3rd year of Yongchu he took the throne at seventeen, changing the era to Jingping, with Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, Xie Hui, and Tan Daoji governing by the late will. The Young Emperor "played endlessly and neglected government": the records show him at play with the palace women, opening a wine shop in the Huayuan park and pricing the wine himself — a young sovereign without an ounce of the sovereign's bearing.

In the 1st year of Jingping Wei came south, and the commanderies of Si, Yan, and Yu mostly fell; the emperor took no heed, leaving the armies and the government to his ministers. In the fifth month of the 2nd year of Jingping, Xu Xianzhi and the others, by the empress dowager's edict, deposed him as Prince of Yingyang, confined him in Wu, and soon had him slain, aged nineteen. With Wu's sons still children, the ministers brought in the Prince of Yidu, Liu Yilong — Emperor Wen.

His deposition opened the southern dynasties' practice of deposition by ministers: for three centuries to come, deposed sovereigns and murdered lords were common, from Xiao Daocheng's slaying of the Later Deposed Emperor to Xiao Luan's deposition of the Princes of Yulin and Hailing. That a young emperor lost his realm to play was his own doing; but the pattern — a child on the throne, strong ministers usurping — began with Liu Song: Wu's jealousy and the Young Emperor's frivolity together colored the politics of the age.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Songshu*, ch. 4 ("Benji of the Young Emperor"), ch. 43 (biography of Xu Xianzhi) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 宋文帝 · 主要事迹

刘义隆字车儿，武帝第三子。少帝被废，义隆自江陵入建康即位，改元元嘉，时年十八。元嘉三年，诛徐羡之、傅亮，讨谢晦于江陵，亲政——元嘉之治，自此始。文帝在位三十年，劝农兴学、简刑省赋，户口蕃息，「余粮栖亩」，「元嘉之治」为南朝唯一的小康之世；元嘉十六年立玄、史、文、儒四学，文化灿然。

然文帝之政，有两失：其一为北伐——元嘉七年到彦之北伐，初复河南，冬复尽失；元嘉二十七年大举北伐，王玄谟败绩，魏太武帝拓跋焘南渡淮水，兵临瓜步，江北涂炭，「元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾」（辛弃疾《永遇乐》），此役使南朝元气大伤。其二为立嗣——文帝久不立太子之母弟彭城王义康，又废杀之；晚年信太子刘劭，终致元嘉三十年二月，太子劭弑帝于合殿，年四十七。

文帝「聪明仁厚，元嘉称治」，然北伐操切、骨肉相残，终以惨祸收场。南朝之君，文帝本为最贤者之一；然「元嘉之治」的底子，被两度北伐与骨肉之祸耗损殆尽——刘宋由盛转衰，实自文帝之世始。

> 本地参考：点校本《宋书》卷005《文帝纪》、卷099《二凶传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Yilong, styled Che'er, was the third son of Emperor Wu. After the Young Emperor's deposition he came from Jiangling to Jiankang, took the throne at eighteen, and changed the era to Yuanjia. In the 3rd year of Yuanjia he slew Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang and marched against Xie Hui at Jiangling — ruling in person, and the Yuanjia recovery began. Thirty years he encouraged farming and learning, lightened the laws and the levies, and the households multiplied; "grain left standing in the fields" — the one era of modest plenty in the southern dynasties. In the 16th year he founded the four academies of Metaphysics, History, Letters, and Confucianism, and culture shone.

His reign had two great errors. The first was the northern expeditions: in the 7th year Dao Yanzhi's campaign recovered Henan, lost again that winter; in the 27th year the great expedition failed — Wang Xuanmo beaten, Emperor Taiwu of Wei crossing the Huai and riding to Guabu, the lands north of the river laid waste. "Yuanjia, in haste, sealed the Wolf's Head and gained a panic flight north" (Xin Qiji) — the south never recovered its strength. The second was the succession: he long refused to fix the succession, destroyed his brother the Prince of Pengcheng, then trusted the heir Liu Shao — until, in the second month of the 30th year of Yuanjia, Shao slew him in the He Hall, aged forty-seven.

"Sharp and benevolent, his Yuanjia years well governed" — yet the expeditions too hasty and kin slaying kin, he ended in catastrophe. Of the southern sovereigns Wen was among the best; but the substance of the Yuanjia recovery was spent on the two expeditions and the family slaughter — the decline of Liu Song began in his own reign.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Songshu*, ch. 5 ("Benji of Emperor Wen"), ch. 99 (the Two Parricides) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 宋孝武帝 · 主要事迹

刘骏字休龙，文帝第三子。元嘉三十年太子刘劭弑文帝，骏时为武陵王，镇江州，起兵讨逆，诛刘劭及其党，即皇帝位，改元孝建——「弑父之贼」为骏所诛，时论称之。然孝武之治，转趋苛暴：孝建元年平南郡王义宣之乱；大明三年竟陵王诞反于广陵，骏讨平之，屠广陵城，「城内男丁皆杀之」——南朝屠城之惨，无过于此。

孝武帝在位十一年，多兴土木，宫室服饰屡变，「私蓄以为常」，赋役繁苛，民不堪命；又猜忌宗室，诸王多遭诛戮。然亦有所建树：裁抑诸王、收刺史之权，中央集权有所加强；又置「典签」以监视诸王，为南朝宗室政治之新制。

大明八年，孝武帝崩，年三十五，前废帝刘子业继。史评孝武：「少机颖，神采爽发」，然「自恃才力，多所诛杀」。南朝宫闱弑立之祸，自孝武之世愈演愈烈——其以讨逆得位，而子业以暴亡继之，刘宋骨肉相残之局，遂不可止。

> 本地参考：点校本《宋书》卷006《孝武帝纪》、卷079《竟陵王诞传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Jun, styled Xiulong, was the third son of Emperor Wen. In the 30th year of Yuanjia the heir Liu Shao slew Emperor Wen; Jun, the Prince of Wuling holding Jiangzhou, rose against him, destroyed Shao and his party, and took the throne, changing the era to Xiaojian — the "parricide" destroyed, and the age applauded. But his rule turned harsh: in the 1st year of Xiaojian he put down the Prince of Nanjun's revolt; in the 3rd year of Daming the Prince of Jingling rose at Guangling, and Jun, having destroyed him, massacred the city — "all the male inhabitants were slain" — the bitterest massacre of the southern dynasties.

Eleven years on the throne, he raised buildings endlessly, changing his palaces and dress, "keeping his own store," and the levies crushed the people; he distrusted the princes and many were done to death. Yet there was method: he clipped the princes' power, gathered the governors' authority to the center, and set the "secretaries of inspection" over the princely courts — a new institution of southern dynastic politics.

He died in the 8th year of Daming at thirty-five; the Former Deposed Emperor Ziye succeeded. The histories say he was "sharp from youth, of brilliant bearing," yet "trusting his own ability, he slew without measure." The slaughters of the southern palace grew worse from his reign on: he won the throne by avenging a parricide, and his son died a tyrant's death — the family wars of Liu Song could not be stopped.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Songshu*, ch. 6 ("Benji of Emperor Xiaowu"), ch. 79 (biography of the Prince of Jingling) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 前废帝 · 主要事迹

刘子业，孝武帝长子，大明八年即位，年十六。前废帝在位一年，为南朝暴君之最：即位之初，改元永光，旋改景和，一年数改元；诛杀大臣宗室——杀戴法兴、刘义恭等，朝野震恐；又「纵恣无度」，荒淫秽乱之事，史不绝书。南史称其「凶悖狂悖，无人君之度」。

景和元年十一月，湘东王刘彧（明帝）与阮佃夫等密谋，使寿寂之等弑帝于华林园，年十七。废帝死后，刘彧即皇帝位。前废帝之暴，使刘宋宗室相残之祸达到顶点：自孝武以来，兄弟叔侄相戕，至废帝一朝，宗室殆尽。

史家论前废帝：「以童昏之质，当凶悖之资」，其暴虐并非个人变态，实为南朝宗室政治之必然产物——自文帝见弑、孝武屠城，刘宋之「骨肉相残」已成本能。前废帝在位一年而亡，刘宋国势自此一蹶不振：其后明帝骨肉相残、后废帝见弑、顺帝禅位，不过二十年间，刘宋遂亡。

> 本地参考：点校本《宋书》卷007《前废帝纪》、卷008《明帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Ziye, eldest son of Emperor Xiaowu, took the throne in the 8th year of Daming at sixteen. His one year on the throne made him the worst tyrant of the southern dynasties: he changed the era from Yongguang to Jinghe within a single year; he slew ministers and princes — Dai Faxing, Liu Yigong, and the rest — until court and realm trembled; and his "unbounded license" and obscenities fill the records. The *Nanshi* calls him "wicked, perverse, without an ounce of the sovereign's bearing."

In the eleventh month of the 1st year of Jinghe, the Prince of Xiangdong, Liu Yu (Emperor Ming), with Ruan Dianfu and the others, had Shou Jizhi slay him in the Hualin Park, aged seventeen; Yu took the throne. His tyranny carried the slaughter of the Song house to its height: from Xiaowu on, brothers and uncles and nephews destroyed each other, and by the Deposed Emperor's reign the princes were nearly gone.

The historians see in him not a monster but the product of the southern palace system: since Emperor Wen's slaying and Xiaowu's massacre, kin slaying kin had become the instinct of Liu Song. One year on the throne, and the state never recovered: under Emperor Ming the family slaughters went on, the Later Deposed Emperor was slain, Emperor Shun abdicated — within twenty years Liu Song was gone.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Songshu*, ch. 7 ("Benji of the Former Deposed Emperor"), ch. 8 ("Benji of Emperor Ming") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 宋明帝 · 主要事迹

刘彧字休炳，文帝第十一子，封湘东王。景和元年，前废帝被弑，彧即位，改元泰始。明帝好读书、善隶书，「有文才」，然承前废帝之乱，即位之初即逢大难：泰始二年，晋安王子勋据江州称帝，四方响应，内战年余，明帝亲征平之——刘宋经此一役，宗室大臣死伤殆尽。

泰始中，明帝乘北魏内乱北伐，然将帅失和，徐、兖、青、冀等州尽入于魏，淮北之地一朝尽失——「淮北尽失」，南朝疆域自此以淮水为界，为南朝国力转折点。明帝晚年，「多忌讳，好猜忍」，诛杀诸弟及功臣，惟恐身后之祸；又因无子而密令嬖幸为诸王「代育」——骨肉相残之惨，有甚于前。

泰豫元年，明帝崩，年三十四，后废帝刘昱即位。史评明帝：「猜忌残忍，末年尤甚。」刘宋自武帝建国至明帝，不过五十余年，而宗室相戕已成常态；明帝之死，刘宋已是强弩之末——其后后废帝见弑、顺帝禅位，萧道成乘隙代宋。

> 本地参考：点校本《宋书》卷008《明帝纪》、卷084《晋安王子勋传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Yu, styled Xiubing, was the eleventh son of Emperor Wen, enfeoffed Prince of Xiangdong. After the Former Deposed Emperor's slaying he took the throne and changed the era to Taishi. A reader and a master of clerical script, "a man of letters," he inherited the ruin: in the 2nd year of Taishi the Prince of Jin'an, Zixun, took the throne at Jiangzhou with half the realm answering, and the civil war ran over a year before the emperor, campaigning in person, put it down — the princes and ministers of Liu Song were nearly spent.

In the mid-Taishi years, with Wei in internal disorder, he campaigned north — but his generals quarreled, and Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji fell to Wei: the Huai north was lost at a stroke, and the southern frontier has run along the Huai ever since — the hinge of the south's decline. In his last years he grew "full of taboos and jealous cruelty," slaying his brothers and his meritorious ministers against the perils to come; and, having no son, he secretly had his favorites "bear children" for the princes — the family slaughter of the age, carried further than ever.

He died in the 1st year of Taiyu at thirty-four; the Later Deposed Emperor Yu succeeded. The histories say: "jealous and cruel, worst of all in his last years." From Wu's founding to Ming, not fifty years, and kin slaying kin was the norm; with Ming's death Liu Song was spent — the Later Deposed Emperor was slain, Emperor Shun abdicated, and Xiao Daocheng took the realm.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Songshu*, ch. 8 ("Benji of Emperor Ming"), ch. 84 (biography of the Prince of Jin'an) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 后废帝 · 主要事迹

刘昱，明帝长子，泰豫元年即位，年十岁。褚渊、袁粲、蔡兴宗、沈攸之、萧道成等受遗辅政。后废帝「无道好杀」：史载其好微行，常夜出游戏，「与左右数人，或骑或步，出郊野」，又虐杀百姓，「击脑捶阴，剖心之酷」，朝野畏之如虎。

元徽二年，桂阳王刘休范反，兵临建康，萧道成等平之，道成威望日隆；元徽五年，后废帝欲杀萧道成，道成先发制人，使心腹杨玉夫等弑帝于仁寿殿，年十五。立安成王刘准，是为顺帝；两年后，萧道成受禅，刘宋亡。

后废帝在位五年，南朝「主少国疑、权臣坐大」之局至此成型：幼主游戏虐杀，权臣弑立自如。萧道成以平乱之威、弑君之名、禅代之实，走完了自刘裕以来「权臣代兴」的标准路径。史家论后废帝：其暴虐虽甚，然以十岁童昏当此局面，实为南朝政治的牺牲品——刘宋之亡，不亡于后废帝一人，而亡于其宗室政治之积弊。

> 本地参考：点校本《宋书》卷009《后废帝纪》、南齐书卷001《高帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Yu, eldest son of Emperor Ming, took the throne in the 1st year of Taiyu at ten, with Chu Yuan, Yuan Can, Cai Xingzong, Shen Youzhi, and Xiao Daocheng governing by the late will. The Later Deposed Emperor was "lawless and fond of killing": the records tell of his secret jaunts by night, "walking or riding into the wilds with a few attendants," and his cruelties against the people — "clubbing heads, gouging hearts" — until court and realm feared him as a beast.

In the 2nd year of Yuanhui the Prince of Guiyang, Xiufan, rose and struck at Jiankang; Xiao Daocheng and the others put it down, and Daocheng's prestige rose daily. In the 5th year of Yuanhui, the emperor moved to kill Daocheng; Daocheng struck first, and his man Yang Yufu slew the emperor in the Renshou Hall, aged fifteen. The Prince of Ancheng, Zhun, was set up — Emperor Shun — and two years later Daocheng received the abdication: Liu Song was no more.

Five years on the throne, and the pattern of "a child sovereign, a doubtful state, strong ministers grown great" was complete: a child playing and killing, ministers deposing and enthroning at will. Daocheng walked the standard road of the southern usurper — merit in pacification, a slain sovereign, an abdication. The histories see the Later Deposed Emperor as no less a victim of the southern system than a monster: the fall of Liu Song was not the work of one child but of the accumulated disease of its princely politics.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Songshu*, ch. 9 ("Benji of the Later Deposed Emperor"), and the *Nanqishu*, ch. 1 ("Benji of Emperor Gao") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 宋顺帝 · 主要事迹

刘准字仲谋，明帝第三子。元徽五年后废帝被弑，萧道成立准即位，年十岁，改元升明。顺帝「幼冲傀儡，身当禅代」：即位后实权尽在萧道成，升明二年荆州沈攸之起兵，道成讨平之，宋室更孤；升明三年三月，萧道成使人讽帝禅位。

禅位诏出，顺帝「泣而升舆」，出宫之时，问左右「今日何不奏鼓吹」——史载其「谓左右曰：愿生生世世，不复生帝王家」，遂禅位于萧道成，刘宋历八帝六十年而亡。顺帝禅后封汝阴王，居丹阳，未几为萧道成使人杀害，年十三。

顺帝之禅，与恭帝之禅、禅汉、禅魏之禅同其轨迹：禅让之名，掩盖篡夺之实；禅后杀之，更见其伪。刘裕代晋而杀恭帝，萧道成代宋而杀顺帝——「禅让」之伪，南朝愈演愈烈。史家论顺帝：以十龄之童，坐视祖业之亡，非其罪也；刘宋之亡，亡于骨肉相残、权臣坐大之积弊久矣。

> 本地参考：点校本《宋书》卷010《顺帝纪》、南齐书卷001《高帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Zhun, styled Zhongmou, was the third son of Emperor Ming. After the Later Deposed Emperor's slaying in the 5th year of Yuanhui, Xiao Daocheng set Zhun on the throne at ten, changing the era to Shengming. Shun was "a child figurehead caught in the abdication": the power lay wholly with Daocheng; in the 2nd year of Shengming Shen Youzhi of Jingzhou rose, Daocheng destroyed him, and the Song house stood more alone than ever. In the third month of the 3rd year of Shengming, Daocheng's men pressed for the abdication.

The edict of abdication made, Shun "wept as he mounted the carriage"; leaving the palace he asked his attendants, "Why is the band not playing today?" — the records have him saying, "In life after life, may I never again be born into an imperial house" — and he yielded to Daocheng: Liu Song, eight sovereigns and sixty years, was no more. Enfeoffed Prince of Ruyin and settled at Danyang, he was soon done to death by Daocheng's men, aged thirteen.

His abdication follows the same road as Gong's, as the abdications of Han and Wei: the name of abdication masking the fact of usurpation, and the abdicated sovereign slain to complete it. Liu Yu took the Jin and slew Emperor Gong; Xiao Daocheng took the Song and slew Emperor Shun — the mask wearing ever thinner. The historians absolve Shun: a ten-year-old watching his grandfather's realm pass, it was not his fault; Liu Song fell to its family slaughters and its overgrown ministers, long before he sat the throne.

# 齐高帝 · 主要事迹

萧道成字绍伯，南兰陵人，萧何之后。仕宋，以军功起家：平竟陵王诞之乱、破桂阳王休范，威名日著。元徽五年，后废帝欲杀道成，道成先发制人，使心腹弑帝，立顺帝；升明二年，讨平荆州沈攸之，遂专朝政。升明三年，顺帝禅位，道成即皇帝位，国号齐，改元建元——刘宋六十载基业，一朝移于萧氏。

高帝在位四年，为政节俭：「身不御精细之物」，尝曰「使我治天下十年，当使黄金与土同价」；定礼仪、设官制，安抚百姓。又置「黄籍」以检户口，整顿户籍之弊。然建元四年，道成崩，年五十六，太子萧赜即位，是为齐武帝。

史评高帝：「沉深有大量，宽严得宜。」以寒门武将取天下，而能俭以守成，在南朝开国之君中，最为难得。然齐祚短促——高帝之节俭未能传之后世，武帝永明之治后，郁林、海陵二世而废，萧鸾篡立，不过二十余年而齐亡。高帝之德，未及三世。

> 本地参考：点校本《南齐书》卷001《高帝纪》、卷002《高帝纪下》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Xiao Daocheng, styled Shaobo, was a man of Nanlanling, claiming descent from Xiao He of Han. He rose by merit under Song: putting down the Prince of Jingling's revolt and breaking the Prince of Guiyang, his name grew daily. In the 5th year of Yuanhui, when the Later Deposed Emperor moved to kill him, he struck first — his men slew the emperor and set up Emperor Shun; in the 2nd year of Shengming he destroyed Shen Youzhi of Jingzhou and held the government alone. In the 3rd year of Shengming, Emperor Shun abdicated: Daocheng took the throne, styled the realm Qi, and changed the era to Jianyuan — sixty years of Liu Song passed to the Xiao house in a day.

Four years he reigned, in frugality: "he would not use fine things," and said, "let me govern the realm ten years, and gold shall be worth no more than earth"; he fixed the rites and the offices and calmed the people; he revised the household registers, mending the abuses of the census. In the 4th year of Jianyuan he died at fifty-six; his heir Xiao Ze succeeded as Emperor Wu.

The histories say of him: "deep and of great measure, lenient and strict in due proportion." A common soldier who took the realm and kept it frugally — the rarest of the southern founders. But the Qi line was brief: his frugality did not outlast his sons; after Wu's Yongming recovery, the Princes of Yulin and Hailing were deposed in turn, Xiao Luan usurped, and within twenty years Qi was gone. Gao's virtue did not reach the third generation.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Nanqishu*, ch. 1 and 2 ("Benji of Emperor Gao") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

The northern campaigns gained nothing, and he died in the 11th year of Yongming.

# 齐武帝 · 主要事迹

萧赜字宣远，高帝长子。建元四年高帝崩，赜即位，年四十二，改元永明。武帝在位十一年，承高帝之俭，行宽和之政：劝农桑、减赋役、简刑罚，又崇儒学、兴学校，百姓丰乐——史称「永明之治」，为南朝继元嘉之后又一小康之世。

永明年间，文化灿然：武帝与竟陵王萧子良开西邸，招揽文士，沈约、谢朓、王融等皆在其列，讲求声律，创「永明体」，为近体诗之滥觞；竟陵八友之盛，冠绝南朝。然永明五年后，齐与北魏缘边相持，北讨无大功；武帝晚年，太子萧长懋（文惠太子）早卒，太孙萧昭业立为储君，「其后少主失德，遂成祸乱」。

永明十一年，武帝崩，年五十四，太孙昭业即位。史评武帝：「留心政事，务从简约」，然「委任群小，朝纲渐弛」。永明之治，为南朝黄金时代之最后余晖：武帝崩后十年，萧鸾篡位、东昏之乱、萧衍代齐，齐祚遂亡——永明之盛，转瞬成空。

> 本地参考：点校本《南齐书》卷003《武帝纪》、卷052《文学传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Xiao Ze, styled Xuanyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Gao. On his father's death in the 4th year of Jianyuan he took the throne at forty-two, changing the era to Yongming. Eleven years he carried on Gao's frugality with a lenient hand: he encouraged farming and mulberries, lightened the levies and the corvée, simplified the punishments, honored the Confucian learning and built the schools — the people prospered, and the "Yongming recovery" became, after Yuanjia, the second era of modest plenty in the southern dynasties.

The Yongming years shone in culture: the emperor and the Prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, opened the western mansion, gathering Shen Yue, Xie Tiao, Wang Rong, and the rest, who worked out the rules of tone — the "Yongming style," fountainhead of the regulated verse. The Eight Friends of the Jingling were the glory of the southern courts. But after the 5th year of Yongming, Qi and Wei held the border without decision, and the north gained nothing; in his last years the Crown Prince Wenhui died early, and his grandson Zhaoye was made heir — "and the young sovereign's misrule followed."

He died in the 11th year of Yongming at fifty-four; his grandson Zhaoye succeeded. The histories say he "attended to government and kept it simple," yet "trusted the petty men, and the court's discipline slackened." The Yongming recovery was the last glow of the southern golden age: within ten years of his death Xiao Luan usurped, the Marquis of Donghun raged, Xiao Yan took the realm — the glory of Yongming passed like a dream.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Nanqishu*, ch. 3 ("Benji of Emperor Wu"), ch. 52 (biographies of the literary men) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 郁林王 · 主要事迹

萧昭业字元尚，文惠太子萧长懋长子，武帝太孙。永明十一年武帝崩，昭业即位，年二十一，改元隆昌。郁林王「轻薄无行」：史载其「与左右群小，通宵达旦，戏狎无度」，又「以钱为戏」，好赌博，朝政尽委西昌侯萧鸾（明帝）。

昭业即位未及一年，宗室萧鸾以辅政之名渐收实权：先杀司徒竟陵王萧子良之党，又诛高帝旧臣；隆昌元年七月，萧鸾以太后令废帝为郁林王，旋使人弑之，年二十二。郁林之废，是齐之「主少国疑」之始：高帝、武帝诸子尚存，而萧鸾以宗室之尊篡立——南朝宗室相残之祸，在萧齐重演。

史家论郁林王：「少美容止，好隶书」，然「性佻巧，荒于色」。以武帝之太孙、文惠之嫡嗣，本应承永明之业；然「幼而失教，长而无度」，终为萧鸾所乘。郁林之亡，为齐祚之转折：自其见废，萧鸾大诛高武诸子，齐之宗室元气尽丧，东昏之乱、萧衍代齐，皆其绪余。

> 本地参考：点校本《南齐书》卷004《郁林王》、卷006《明帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Xiao Zhaoye, styled Yuanshang, was the eldest son of the Crown Prince Wenhui and Emperor Wu's grandson. On Wu's death in the 11th year of Yongming he took the throne at twenty-one, changing the era to Longchang. The Prince of Yulin was "frivolous and worthless": the records tell of his "nightlong play with the palace boys," his gambling, his "money games," while the government fell to the Marquis of Xichang, Xiao Luan (Emperor Ming).

Within a year of his accession Luan, governing in his name, gathered the power: first he destroyed the party of the Prince of Jingling, then the old ministers of Emperor Gao; in the seventh month of the 1st year of Longchang, by the empress dowager's edict, he deposed Zhaoye as Prince of Yulin and soon had him slain, aged twenty-two. His deposition opened Qi's "child sovereign, doubtful state": with the sons of Gao and Wu still living, a senior prince usurped — the family wars of the southern courts replaying in Qi.

The histories say of him: "handsome in his youth, a master of clerical script," yet "artful and dissolute, reckless in pleasure." The grandson of Wu, the heir of Wenhui, he should have carried on the Yongming recovery; but "untaught in childhood, ungoverned in youth," he was seized by Luan. His fall was the hinge of the Qi line: after it, Luan slaughtered the sons of Gao and Wu, the princes' strength was spent, and the Marquis of Donghun's ruin and Xiao Yan's succession were but its aftermath.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Nanqishu*, ch. 4 (the Prince of Yulin), ch. 6 ("Benji of Emperor Ming") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 海陵王 · 主要事迹

萧昭文，文惠太子次子，郁林王弟。隆昌元年，萧鸾废郁林王，立昭文为帝，改元延兴——昭文在位数月而已。延兴元年七月，萧鸾再废昭文为海陵王，自立为帝，改元建武；海陵王旋为萧鸾使人杀害，年十五。

海陵之立，纯为萧鸾篡位之过渡：废一帝、立一帝、再废之，皆在数月之间。昭文「幼冲傀儡」，史载其在位时「萧鸾专决国政，帝拱手而已」；其被废时，「依高帝例，给鼓吹一部」，黯然出宫。海陵王虽入齐帝序列，然在位之短、之傀儡，为南朝诸帝之最。

史家论海陵：「以冲年践祚，国柄已移。」齐祚自高帝开国至海陵见废，不过十六年——萧鸾以宗室行篡立之事，废两帝、杀两帝（郁林、海陵），其凶残有甚于宋之萧道成。海陵之短祚，正反映南朝「权臣废立」之常态：天子之位，沦为权臣掌中之物。

> 本地参考：点校本《南齐书》卷005《海陵王》、卷006《明帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Xiao Zhaowen, second son of the Crown Prince Wenhui and younger brother of the Prince of Yulin, was set up as emperor by Xiao Luan after the Yulin deposition in the 1st year of Longchang, changing the era to Yanxing — and reigned a few months. In the seventh month of the 1st year of Yanxing, Luan deposed him in turn as Prince of Hailing and took the throne himself, changing the era to Jianwu; the prince was soon done to death, aged fifteen.

His enthronement was pure transition for Luan's usurpation: one emperor deposed, another set up, another deposed — all within months. Zhaowen, "a child figurehead," sat while "Luan decided everything, the emperor folding his hands"; on his deposition he was "granted a band of music, after the precedent of Emperor Gao," and left the palace in the dusk. Though he stands in the Qi imperial sequence, his reign was the shortest and the most puppet-like of the southern sovereigns.

The historians say: "A child on the throne, and the realm's power was already gone." From Gao's founding to Hailing's deposition was but sixteen years; Luan, usurping as a senior prince, deposed two emperors and slew both (Yulin and Hailing) — cruelty beyond Xiao Daocheng's. Hailing's brief reign reflects the southern norm: the throne itself had become a thing in the strong minister's hand.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Nanqishu*, ch. 5 (the Prince of Hailing), ch. 6 ("Benji of Emperor Ming") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 齐明帝 · 主要事迹

萧鸾字景栖，高帝侄，始安贞王萧道生之子。仕宋、齐两朝，以宗室之尊、吏干之才历任要职。建武元年，鸾废海陵王自立，改元建武——齐之高武子孙，从此尽在刀俎。明帝在位四年，「大诛宗室」：高帝十九子、武帝诸子，杀之殆尽，「高武子孙，遂无遗类」，史称其「惨毒」。

明帝之治，尚有吏干：整顿户籍、核实户口、减免赋役，政事颇有条理；建武四年，北魏孝文帝大举南伐，明帝遣军拒之，齐边告急而未致大败。然其猜忌成性，「深自藏匿」，以「典签」监视诸王，暮年尤甚，因无子而密令宠妃「代育」——骨肉相残，无所不用其极。

永泰元年，明帝崩，年四十七，子萧宝卷（东昏侯）即位。史评明帝：「有吏才而多猜忌，以诛戮为威。」萧鸾以宗室篡立、屠戮高武子孙，虽一时得逞，然其子东昏侯暴虐更甚，萧衍起兵，不过三年而齐亡——明帝之「惨毒」，实为齐祚速亡之直接原因。

> 本地参考：点校本《南齐书》卷006《明帝纪》、卷035《高帝诸子传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Xiao Luan, styled Jingqi, was a nephew of Emperor Gao, son of Xiao Daosheng, Prince Zhen of Shian. Serving both Song and Qi, he held the highest offices as a senior prince of tested ability. In the 1st year of Jianwu he deposed the Prince of Hailing and took the throne himself — and from that day the sons of Gao and Wu were under the knife. Four years he reigned, "slaughtering the princes": of Gao's nineteen sons and Wu's sons, nearly all were destroyed, "so that no descendant of Gao and Wu remained" — the histories call it poison.

Yet he had administrative talent: he revised the registers, verified the households, lightened the levies, and kept the government in order; in the 4th year of Jianwu, when Emperor Xiaowen of Wei marched south in force, he held the line and the border, though in peril, did not break. But his jealousy was a disease: "hiding himself deep," he set the secretaries of inspection over the princes, and in his last years, having no son, had his favorites "bear children" for him — the family cruelty carried to its last extreme.

He died in the 1st year of Yongtai at forty-seven; his son Baojuan, the Marquis of Donghun, succeeded. The histories say: "administrative ability with boundless jealousy, ruling by slaughter." A senior prince who usurped and butchered the sons of Gao and Wu, he held his throne a while — but his son's tyranny was worse, Xiao Yan rose, and within three years Qi was gone: his "poison" was the direct cause of the realm's swift fall.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Nanqishu*, ch. 6 ("Benji of Emperor Ming"), ch. 35 (biographies of Gao's sons) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 东昏侯 · 主要事迹

萧宝卷，明帝次子。永泰元年明帝崩，宝卷即位，年十六，改元永元。东昏侯为南朝暴君之最：史载其「好戏狎」，性残忍，即位即诛杀大臣——杀徐孝嗣、陈显达等，又「凿金为莲花以帖地，令潘妃行其上，曰此步步生莲花也」，金莲之奢、潘妃之宠，传为千古谈资。

永元年间，宝卷「深居简出」，不理朝政，亲信茹法珍、梅虫儿等弄权；又滥杀宗室功臣，萧衍（时为雍州刺史）起兵襄阳，东下讨逆。中兴元年，萧衍军入建康，宝卷被废为东昏侯，旋为部将所杀，年十九——南齐高武之业，至此而斩。

史家论东昏侯：「性讷涩，少言」，然「凶暴奢虐，无所不为」。齐自高帝立国，历七帝二十四年而亡——其中明帝篡立、大诛宗室，东昏暴虐、众叛亲离，萧衍代齐，不过顺势而已。东昏之亡，为南朝「暴君速亡」之又一例：其金莲之奢、诛戮之暴，皆成后世殷鉴。

> 本地参考：点校本《南齐书》卷007《东昏侯》、梁书卷001《武帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Xiao Baojuan, second son of Emperor Ming, took the throne in the 1st year of Yongtai at sixteen, changing the era to Yongyuan. The Marquis of Donghun was the worst tyrant of the southern dynasties: the records tell of his "love of play," his cruelty; on the throne he slew his ministers — Xu Xiaosi, Chen Xianda, and the rest — and "had gold beaten into lotus petals to pave the ground, and made Consort Pan walk on them, saying, 'with every step a lotus grows.'" The golden lotus and the favorite Pan passed into legend.

In the Yongyuan years he "kept himself hidden," leaving the government to the favorites Ru Fazhen and Mei Chong'er; he slew princes and meritorious ministers without measure, until Xiao Yan, the Governor of Yongzhou, rose from Xiangyang and marched east to punish him. In the 1st year of Zhongxing Yan's army entered Jiankang; Baojuan was degraded as Marquis of Donghun and slain by his own officers, aged nineteen — the enterprise of Gao and Wu was cut off.

The histories say: "of slow speech, keeping to himself," yet "cruel, extravagant, and lawless beyond measure." From Gao's founding, Qi ran seven sovereigns and twenty-four years — Luan's usurpation and the princes' slaughter, the Marquis's tyranny and the realm's desertion: Xiao Yan's succession was only the last step. The Marquis's fall is another instance of the southern tyrant's swift ruin; the golden lotus and the slaughter remain the eternal warning.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Nanqishu*, ch. 7 (the Marquis of Donghun), and the *Liangshu*, ch. 1 ("Benji of Emperor Wu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 齐和帝 · 主要事迹

萧宝融，明帝第八子，封南康王。永元二年，萧衍起兵襄阳，次年奉宝融即位于江陵，改元中兴，遥尊建康之东昏侯为「废帝」——齐之南北二帝并立。中兴元年，萧衍军克建康，杀东昏侯；中兴二年三月，萧衍使人讽和帝禅位。

禅位诏下，和帝逊位，封巴陵王；未几，萧衍使人杀之，年十五——齐历七帝二十四年而亡，梁武帝萧衍立国。和帝以幼冲之年，为萧衍拥立与废杀，其遭遇与宋顺帝如出一辙：禅让之名，篡夺之实，禅后杀之，南朝之「禅代」至此已成定式。

史家论和帝：「以幼冲之质，处危疑之位」，其禅位与遇害，皆非其罪。南朝宋、齐、梁、陈四代，开国者皆以「禅让」取天下，而禅后之君多遭杀害：晋恭帝、宋顺帝、齐和帝，皆不得善终——「禅让」二字之伪，在南朝暴露无遗。齐祚虽短，而萧梁继之，南朝历史进入梁武帝之世。

> 本地参考：点校本《南齐书》卷008《和帝纪》、梁书卷001《武帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Xiao Baorong, eighth son of Emperor Ming, enfeoffed Prince of Nankang. In the 2nd year of Yongyuan Xiao Yan rose from Xiangyang, and the next year set Baorong on the throne at Jiangling, changing the era to Zhongxing and styling the Marquis of Donghun in Jiankang "the deposed emperor" — Qi had two sovereigns at once. In the 1st year of Zhongxing Yan's army took Jiankang and slew the Marquis; in the third month of the 2nd year of Zhongxing, Yan's men pressed for the abdication.

The edict made, Emperor He yielded, enfeoffed Duke of Baling; within days Yan's men did him to death, aged fifteen — Qi, seven sovereigns and twenty-four years, was no more, and Xiao Yan founded Liang. A child enthroned and slain by Xiao Yan, his fate mirrors Emperor Shun of Song: the name of abdication masking the usurpation, the abdicated sovereign slain to complete it — the southern "abdication" had become a fixed ritual.

The histories absolve him: "a child in a perilous seat," his abdication and his death were not his doing. The four southern dynasties — Song, Qi, Liang, Chen — all took the realm by "abdication," and most of the abdicated sovereigns were murdered: Emperor Gong of Jin, Emperor Shun of Song, Emperor He of Qi — none died in his bed. The falseness of "abdication" was exposed to the full in the southern courts. Qi was brief, but Liang followed, and the age passed to Emperor Wu of Liang.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Nanqishu*, ch. 8 ("Benji of Emperor He"), and the *Liangshu*, ch. 1 ("Benji of Emperor Wu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 梁武帝 · 主要事迹

萧衍是梁朝的开国之君。中兴元年（501），他自襄阳东下攻入建康，掌控南齐残局；次年受齐禅即帝位，梁朝由此建立，仍都建康。此后在位近半个世纪，是本图鉴中治世最长的皇帝之一。

开国之初，他置五经博士、振兴文教；天监至大同间长年安定，文学、佛学、礼乐并盛，被推为南朝文化的高峰之一。对外则有天监十三年（514）的浮山堰工程，堰淮水以攻魏，规模巨大而备受争议。

他的另一面是佞佛。大通元年（527）起，同泰寺佛事不断升级，他屡次舍身入寺，由群臣以钱奉赎，佛事与国家财政就此绑定。

晚年的转折在太清元年（547）：侯景来降，纳降之议争论激烈，他最终决定接受。次年侯景之乱爆发，建康遭灾，台城被围；太清三年（549）台城陷落，武帝为侯景所制，忧愤饥病而崩。简文帝随后继位，侯景仍控建康。前半英主、后半困于佛与侯景，正是本朝月旦的两面。

与[[n-wei-xiaowen|北魏孝文帝]]对读：一北一南，一个以汉化改革重铸北魏，一个以文教与佛事撑起南朝文化高峰；而台城之困，则为南朝由盛转衰写下注脚。

bio_parts_en.value:
Xiao Yan was the founding ruler of the Liang dynasty. In Zhongxing 1 (501) he marched east from Xiangyang, stormed Jiankang, and seized control of Southern Qi's endgame; the next year he accepted Qi's abdication and took the throne, founding Liang with the capital still at Jiankang. He would reign for nearly half a century—one of the longest reigns in this atlas.

At the founding he appointed Erudites of the Five Classics and revived letters and learning; the long stability from Tianjian to Datong brought literature, Buddhist learning, and ritual music to a simultaneous flowering, counted among the cultural peaks of the Southern Dynasties. In foreign ventures there was the Fushan Weir project of Tianjian 13 (514), damming the Huai River to attack Wei—a vast and deeply controversial work.

His other face was his devotion to Buddhism. From Datong 1 (527) the rites at Tongtai Temple escalated steadily; he repeatedly surrendered himself to the temple and was ransomed by his officials at great price, binding Buddhist ceremony to the state treasury.

The late-reign turning point came in Taiqing 1 (547): Hou Jing came offering his allegiance, and though the debate over accepting him was fierce, Xiao Yan finally decided to take him in. The next year the Hou Jing Rebellion erupted, disaster struck Jiankang, and Taicheng was besieged; in Taiqing 3 (549) Taicheng fell, and Emperor Wu, held under Hou Jing's control, died of grief, hunger, and illness. Emperor Jianwen succeeded him while Hou Jing still held Jiankang. The able ruler of the first half, the man trapped by Buddha and Hou Jing in the second—these are the two faces of the verdict on his reign.

Read alongside

: one north, one south; one recast Northern Wei through sinicizing reform, the other sustained a Southern Dynasties cultural peak through letters and Buddhist devotion. And the siege of Taicheng wrote the footnote to the Southern Dynasties' turn from height to decline.

emperors.bio_md:
# 梁简文帝 · 主要事迹

萧纲字世缵，武帝第三子，昭明太子萧统之弟。天监二年生，幼聪睿，六岁便能属文。封晋安王，历任刺史，与徐摛、庾肩吾等为文友，倡「宫体诗」——以描写宫廷生活与女性情态为尚，文风绮艳，为南朝文学一大流派。太清三年，侯景陷台城，武帝饿死，纲即位，改元大宝。

简文在位二年，为侯景傀儡：景自为相国、宇宙大将军，专决朝政，帝拱手而已。大宝二年，景废帝为晋安王，幽于永福省，旋使人弑之，年四十九。临终犹赋诗自哀，「南史」载其「读书万卷，犹有今日」之叹。

简文以文士之质，当亡国之运：其宫体诗开齐梁绮丽之风气，为唐诗之先声；然「文雅有余，遭乱不能振」，坐视社稷倾覆而无能为力。侯景之乱为南朝由盛转衰之枢纽，简文不过其间一牺牲品——「南朝四百八十寺」之盛，至此而尽。

> 本地参考：点校本《梁书》卷004《简文帝纪》、卷056《侯景传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Xiao Gang, styled Shizuan, was the third son of Emperor Wu, younger brother of the Crown Prince Zhaoming. Born in the 2nd year of Tianjian, he was sharp from infancy, writing prose at six. Enfeoffed Prince of Jin'an, he served as governor and formed a circle with Xu Chi and Yu Jianwu, championing the "palace style" — a poetry of court life and feminine grace, ornate and sensuous, one of the great schools of southern literature. In the 3rd year of Taiqing, Hou Jing took the palace; Emperor Wu starved to death, and Gang took the throne, changing the era to Dabao.

Two years he reigned as Jing's puppet: Jing made himself chancellor and "Grand General of the Universe," deciding everything while the emperor folded his hands. In the 2nd year of Dabao Jing degraded him as Prince of Jin'an, confined him in the Yongfu Hall, and soon had him slain, aged forty-nine. To the end he wrote poems of his own sorrow; the *Nanshi* records his cry, "I have read ten thousand books, and yet this day."

A man of letters on a dying throne: his palace style opened the sensuous poetry of the Qi–Liang age, the herald of Tang verse; but "letters in plenty, and in the storm he could not rise" — he watched the altars fall without the power to move. The Hou Jing rebellion was the hinge of the southern decline, and Jianwen was but its victim: the age of "four hundred eighty temples in the southern land" was at an end.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Liangshu*, ch. 4 ("Benji of Emperor Jianwen"), ch. 56 (biography of Hou Jing) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 豫章王栋 · 主要事迹

萧栋，昭明太子萧统之孙，豫章王萧欢之子。大宝二年，侯景废简文帝，立栋为帝，改元天正。栋幼弱，本无君人之量，立为帝后「与妇共食，以纸为书」，侯景视之如儿戏——其在位数月，国政一决于景。

天正元年，侯景逼栋禅位，自称汉帝，栋退为淮阴王，幽于永福省。承圣元年，王僧辩、陈霸先等讨平侯景；萧栋兄弟被放出，方以为得生，梁元帝萧绎使人以「侯景余党」之名收而杀之——「南史」记栋兄弟临刑之惨，年皆不过二十。

栋之立与废，皆侯景掌中之物：以昭明之孙入梁帝序列，实为乱世傀儡之极致。图鉴以其名分存于梁统而列为准帝。史家论栋：「幼弱无权，身不由己。」侯景之乱中，梁室宗亲之遭际，无一幸免——栋不过其中最无辜者之一。

> 本地参考：点校本《梁书》卷056《侯景传》、南史卷053《昭明太子诸子传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Xiao Dong was the grandson of the Crown Prince Zhaoming, son of Xiao Huan, Prince of Yuzhang. In the 2nd year of Dabao, Hou Jing deposed Emperor Jianwen and set up Dong, changing the era to Tianzheng. Dong was young and weak, with no bearing of a sovereign; once on the throne, the records say, "he ate with his wife and wrote on paper," while Jing played with him as with a child — his months of reign were decided wholly by Jing.

In the 1st year of Tianzheng Jing forced Dong to abdicate and took the throne himself as Emperor of Han, reducing Dong to Prince of Huaiyin, confined in the Yongfu Hall. In the 1st year of Chengsheng, Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian destroyed Hou Jing; the brothers Dong were released and thought themselves saved — but Emperor Yuan of Liang had them seized as "remnants of Hou Jing's party" and slain, none of them past twenty, as the *Nanshi* records their last hours with pity.

Dong's enthronement and his fall were both Hou Jing's toys: the grandson of Zhaoming in the Liang imperial sequence, in fact the extreme of the age's puppetry. The gazetteer keeps him in the Liang line as quasi-emperor. The historians say: "young, weak, powerless — not his own master." In the Hou Jing storm none of the Liang princes escaped; Dong was only the most innocent of them.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Liangshu*, ch. 56 (biography of Hou Jing), and the *Nanshi*, ch. 53 (the sons of Zhaoming) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 梁元帝 · 主要事迹

萧绎字世诚，武帝第七子，封湘东王。少聪悟好学，「博综群书」，著《金楼子》等，聚书十四万卷，为南朝藏书之最。侯景之乱中，绎以荆州刺史之身，与王僧辩等讨伐侯景；承圣元年，王僧辩克建康、平侯景，绎即位于江陵，改元承圣——梁室中兴，然都于江陵而不还建康，为后来之祸。

元帝在位三年：承圣二年，武陵王萧纪称帝蜀中，元帝遣军讨平之；然其猜忌骨肉，杀其兄邵陵王纶，兄弟相残之惨，甚于侯景。承圣三年，西魏遣于谨等五路南下，破江陵；元帝出降，旋被俘杀，年四十七。城破之时，元帝「尽焚图书」，十四万卷典籍付之一炬——「江陵焚书」，为中国文化史上最大浩劫之一。

元帝聪悟好学而多猜忌，史评「失在不能早复建康」：侯景乱平，梁室应以建康为本，而元帝偏安江陵、自残骨肉，终致西魏乘虚而入。梁之亡，不亡于侯景，而亡于元帝之猜忌与短视；江陵之火，更烧尽了南朝百余年的文化积累。

> 本地参考：点校本《梁书》卷005《元帝纪》、周书卷015《于谨传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Xiao Yi, styled Shicheng, was the seventh son of Emperor Wu, enfeoffed Prince of Xiangdong. Sharp and studious from youth, "learned in all the books," he wrote the *Jinlouzi* and gathered a library of 140,000 volumes — the greatest collection of the southern courts. In the Hou Jing storm, as Governor of Jingzhou, he joined Wang Sengbian against Jing; in the 1st year of Chengsheng Sengbian took Jiankang and destroyed Hou Jing, and Yi took the throne at Jiangling, changing the era to Chengsheng — the restoration of Liang, but a restoration seated at Jiangling instead of Jiankang, and that was the seed of disaster.

Three years he reigned: in the 2nd year of Chengsheng his brother the Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ji, took the throne in Shu, and Yuan destroyed him; but his jealousy of his kin was worse than Hou Jing's — he slew his brother the Prince of Shaoling, and the family slaughter outdid the rebellion. In the 3rd year of Chengsheng Western Wei sent Yujin and the others south on five roads and broke Jiangling; the emperor surrendered and was taken and slain, aged forty-seven. As the city fell, Yuan "burned all his books" — 140,000 volumes in one fire: the Jiangling book-burning, one of the great calamities of Chinese culture.

Sharp and studious but steeped in jealousy, the historians say "his error was not returning to Jiankang in time": with the rebellion ended, the Liang house should have stood on Jiankang, but Yuan hugged Jiangling and slew his kin until Western Wei struck through the gap. Liang fell not to Hou Jing but to Yuan's jealousy and his short sight; and the fire of Jiangling burned away the culture that a hundred years of the southern courts had built.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Liangshu*, ch. 5 ("Benji of Emperor Yuan"), and the *Zhoushu*, ch. 15 (biography of Yujin) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 梁敬帝 · 主要事迹

萧方智，元帝第九子。承圣三年江陵陷、元帝遇害，方智时为晋安王，被迎至建康，绍泰元年即皇帝位，年十三。其时梁室名存实亡：北齐扶植贞阳侯萧渊明，王僧辩一度迎立之，陈霸先袭杀王僧辩，复立方智——建康政柄，已在陈霸先之手。

敬帝在位三年：太平元年，陈霸先拒北齐军于建康，江东稍定；太平二年十月，陈霸先受禅称帝，梁亡。方智禅后封江阴王，次年（永定二年）为陈霸先使人杀害，年十六。梁自武帝开国，历五帝五十六年而亡。

敬帝「幼冲当乱，身当禅代」：其即位、其禅位、其遇害，皆身不由己。梁亡之后，南朝之局转入陈霸先之手——陈祚仅三十三年，为南朝之最短者。史家论敬帝：以十三龄幼主坐视祖业之亡，非其罪也；梁之亡，亡于侯景之乱与宗室相残，积弊久矣。

> 本地参考：点校本《梁书》卷006《敬帝纪》、陈书卷001《高祖纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Xiao Fangzhi, ninth son of Emperor Yuan, was Prince of Jin'an when Jiangling fell in the 3rd year of Chengsheng and Emperor Yuan was slain. Brought to Jiankang, he took the throne in the 1st year of Shaotai at thirteen. Liang was now a name only: Northern Qi propped up the Marquis of Zhenyang, Xiao Yuanming, and Wang Sengbian for a time received him; Chen Baxian struck down Sengbian and restored Fangzhi — the power of Jiankang was already Baxian's.

Three years he reigned: in the 1st year of Taiping Baxian held the Qi armies at Jiankang and Jiangdong was roughly settled; in the tenth month of the 2nd year of Taiping Baxian received the abdication — Liang was no more. Fangzhi, enfeoffed Prince of Jiangyin, was done to death by Baxian's men the next year (the 2nd of Yongding), aged sixteen. From Emperor Wu's founding, Liang ran five sovereigns and fifty-six years.

"Caught in the storm as a child, caught in the abdication": his accession, his abdication, and his death were all beyond his choosing. After Liang fell, the southern stage passed to Chen Baxian — and Chen lasted but thirty-three years, the briefest of the southern dynasties. The historians absolve Fangzhi: a thirteen-year-old watching his grandfather's realm pass was not the cause; Liang fell to the Hou Jing rebellion and the family slaughter, the disease long planted.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Liangshu*, ch. 6 ("Benji of Emperor Jing"), and the *Chenshu*, ch. 1 ("Benji of Emperor Gao") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 陈武帝 · 主要事迹

陈霸先字兴国，吴兴长城人。出身寒微，「少倜傥有大志」，初为里司，后以军功起家，累迁至交州刺史。侯景之乱起，霸先从广州起兵，与王僧辩会师讨侯景，太清三年入建康，平景之乱——「再造梁室」，霸先与僧辩之功居多。

绍泰元年，王僧辩迎立北齐所扶之贞阳侯萧渊明，霸先反对，袭杀僧辩于石头城，复立晋安王方智，自专朝政；太平元年，击退北齐军队于建康近郊，江东得以保全。永定元年，梁敬帝禅位，霸先即皇帝位，国号陈，改元永定——南朝四代之中，陈祚最短，而开国之艰，无过于此。

武帝在位三年，永定三年崩，年五十七。陈朝立国于侯景之乱后，「江左疮痍」，霸先「以寒族之身，取天下于乱世」，然享祚短促，储嗣未定，赖其侄陈蒨（文帝）继之。史评霸先：「英略雄图，豁达大度」，以讨侯景、拒北齐两事，足为南朝后期之柱石。

陈霸先字兴国，吴兴长城人。出身寒微，「少倜傥有大志」，初为里司，后以军功起家，累迁至交州刺史。侯景之乱起，霸先从广州起兵，与王僧辩会师讨侯景，太清三年入建康，平景之乱——「再造梁室」，霸先与僧辩之功居多。

绍泰元年，王僧辩迎立北齐所扶之贞阳侯萧渊明，霸先反对，袭杀僧辩于石头城，复立晋安王方智，自专朝政；太平元年，击退北齐军队于建康近郊，江东得以保全。永定元年，梁敬帝禅位，霸先即皇帝位，国号陈，改元永定——南朝四代之中，陈祚最短，而开国之艰，无过于此。

武帝在位三年，永定三年崩，年五十七。陈朝立国于侯景之乱后，「江左疮痍」，霸先「以寒族之身，取天下于乱世」，然享祚短促，储嗣未定，赖其侄陈蒨（文帝）继之。史评霸先：「英略雄图，豁达大度」，以讨侯景、拒北齐两事，足为南朝后期之柱石。

bio_parts_en.value:
Chen Baxian, styled Xingguo, was a man of Changcheng in Wuxing, of common birth — "unconventional from youth and great of purpose" — who began as a village head and rose by merit of arms to be Governor of Jiaozhou. When the Hou Jing rebellion broke, he rose from Guangzhou and joined Wang Sengbian against Jing, entering Jiankang in the 3rd year of Taiqing to destroy the rebel: the "restoration of the Liang house" was chiefly the work of Baxian and Sengbian.

In the 1st year of Shaotai, when Sengbian received the Marquis of Zhenyang propped up by Qi, Baxian opposed it, struck Sengbian down at Stone City, restored the Prince of Jin'an, and took the government himself; in the 1st year of Taiping he drove the Qi armies back at Jiankang, and Jiangdong was saved. In the 1st year of Yongding Emperor Jing abdicated; Baxian took the throne, styled the realm Chen, and changed the era — of the four southern dynasties, Chen's years were the fewest and its founding the hardest.

Three years he reigned, dying in the 3rd year of Yongding at fifty-seven. Chen stood on ground laid waste by the Hou Jing storm — "the south of the river in ruins" — and Baxian, a common man, took the realm from chaos; but his reign was brief and the succession unsecured, until his nephew Chen Qian (Emperor Wen) carried on. The histories say of him: "of heroic strategy and open measure" — the pillar of the southern courts' last age for two deeds, the destruction of Hou Jing and the holding of the Qi.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Chenshu*, ch. 1 and 2 ("Benji of Emperor Gao") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 陈文帝 · 主要事迹

陈蒨字子华，始兴昭烈王陈道谭长子，武帝陈霸先之侄。武帝无子，永定三年崩，蒨入继大统，即皇帝位，改元天嘉。文帝有武略：天嘉元年，王琳引北齐之兵南下，文帝遣侯瑱等破之，王琳败走，陈疆稍定；又平留异、陈宝应等割据势力，江南复归一统。

文帝在位七年，劝农省役、整顿户籍，「江左经侯景之乱，民户凋残，帝以宽简治之」，史称「天嘉称治」——陈朝之小康，惟文帝之世。其治虽不及宋之元嘉、齐之永明，然在陈祚三十三年中，已为最善者。

天康元年，文帝崩，年四十五，子伯宗即位，是为废帝。史评文帝：「有武略，能保江表。」陈朝地狭力弱，介于北齐、北周之间，文帝以宽简之政、武略之才，为陈朝赢得十余年安定——惜其早逝，嗣子幼弱，宣帝废侄自立，陈之基业，自此转衰。

> 本地参考：点校本《陈书》卷003《世祖纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Chen Qian, styled Zihua, was the eldest son of Xiao Daotan, Prince Zhaolie of Shixing, and nephew of the founder Chen Baxian. Baxian had no son; on his death in the 3rd year of Yongding, Qian succeeded, changing the era to Tianjia. Wen had real military ability: in the 1st year of Tianjia, Wang Lin came south with the Qi armies, and the emperor's general Hou Zhen broke him, Wang Lin fleeing — Chen's borders were roughly fixed; he then put down the separatist lords Liu Yi and Chen Baoying, and the south of the river was one again.

Seven years he reigned, urging farming and lightening corvée, repairing the registers — "after the Hou Jing storm the households of the river were ruined, and the emperor governed them with leniency and simplicity," the histories calling the Tianjia years well governed. It was not the Yuanjia or the Yongming recovery, but in Chen's thirty-three years it was the best.

He died in the 1st year of Tiankang at forty-five; his son Bozong, the Deposed Emperor, succeeded. The histories say: "of real military ability, he held the south of the river." Cramped between Northern Qi and Northern Zhou, Chen won a decade of peace through his lenient government and his martial gifts — pity he died early, leaving a child heir; his brother Xuan deposed the child, and the foundations of Chen turned toward decline.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Chenshu*, ch. 3 ("Benji of Emperor Wen") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 陈废帝 · 主要事迹

陈伯宗，文帝长子。天康元年文帝崩，伯宗即位，年十三，改元光大。废帝「幼弱，政出叔父」：文帝之弟安成王陈顼（宣帝）以太后之兄辅政，进司徒、录尚书事，专决朝政；光大元年，顼诛其党羽刘师知、到仲举等，朝权尽归一人。

光大二年，陈顼以太后令废帝为临海王，自即皇帝位，改元太建——陈之「兄终弟及」之例，自此而开。废帝被废后居临海，太建二年薨，年十七，或云为宣帝所害。

史家论废帝：「幼弱，权在安成。」以十三龄冲主当强叔之朝，废立之柄操于他人，身不由己。南朝宗室相残之局，至陈而不改：宣帝以废侄得位，其后主叔宝之亡，亦不出二十年。废帝之遭遇，与宋之少帝、齐之郁林、海陵如出一辙——「主少国疑」，为南朝政治之痼疾。

> 本地参考：点校本《陈书》卷004《废帝纪》、卷005《宣帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Chen Bozong, eldest son of Emperor Wen, took the throne on his father's death in the 1st year of Tiankang at thirteen, changing the era to Guangda. The Deposed Emperor was "young and weak, the government his uncle's": the Prince of Ancheng, Chen Xu (Emperor Xuan), his father's younger brother, governed as regent and grand secretary, deciding everything; in the 1st year of Guangda he slew the regents Liu Shizhi and Dao Zhongju, and the whole government passed to one man.

In the 2nd year of Guangda, Xu, by the empress dowager's edict, deposed Bozong as Prince of Linhai and took the throne himself, changing the era to Taijian — Chen's practice of brother succeeding brother began here. The deposed emperor lived at Linhai and died in the 2nd year of Taijian at seventeen, some say by Xuan's hand.

The historians say: "young and weak, the power with the Prince of Ancheng." A thirteen-year-old before a strong uncle, his fate was decided for him. The family wars of the southern courts ran on into Chen: Xuan won the throne by deposing his nephew, and his son the Last Sovereign lost the realm within twenty years. The Deposed Emperor's fate matches the Young Emperor of Song and the Princes of Yulin and Hailing of Qi — "a child sovereign, a doubtful state," the old disease of the south.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Chenshu*, ch. 4 ("Benji of the Deposed Emperor"), ch. 5 ("Benji of Emperor Xuan") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 陈宣帝 · 主要事迹

陈顼字绍世，始兴昭烈王第二子，文帝陈蒨之弟。光大二年，废侄伯宗自立，改元太建。宣帝在位十四年，为陈朝武功最盛之世：太建五年，遣吴明彻等北伐，大破北齐，尽复淮南之地，「陈之疆域，于此为最」；又遣使与北周通好，南朝之势，一时复振。

太建九年，北周灭北齐，陈争徐、兖之地；太建十年，吴明彻攻彭城，兵败吕梁，为北周所擒——「吕梁之败」，陈之精锐尽丧，淮南之地复失。宣帝「志在河南，功败垂成」：若能于北齐将亡之时早定方略，或可争中原；然陈力已竭，自此不复北上。

太建十四年，宣帝崩，年五十三，子叔宝即位，是为陈后主。史评宣帝：「有宏略，而识见不远。」陈朝之兴，兴于宣帝之北伐；陈朝之衰，衰于吕梁之败——其与北齐北周之博弈，终不敌北朝之强。宣帝崩后八年，隋灭陈，南朝终。

> 本地参考：点校本《陈书》卷005《宣帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Chen Xu, styled Shaoshi, was the second son of the Prince Zhaolie of Shixing and younger brother of Emperor Wen. In the 2nd year of Guangda he deposed his nephew Bozong and took the throne, changing the era to Taijian. His fourteen years were the height of Chen's arms: in the 5th year of Taijian he sent Wu Mingche and the others north, broke Northern Qi, and recovered all the Huainan — "the widest borders of Chen"; he sent envoys to Northern Zhou in friendship, and the southern power stood up again for a moment.

In the 9th year of Taijian Northern Zhou destroyed Northern Qi, and Chen contended for Xu and Yan; in the 10th year Wu Mingche attacked Pengcheng and was shattered at Lüliang, taken by Zhou — the Lüliang disaster cost Chen its finest troops, and the Huainan was lost again. Xuan's "aim was Henan, the enterprise failed at the last step": had he fixed his strategy when Qi was dying, he might have contended for the Central Plains; but Chen's strength was spent, and it never marched north again.

He died in the 14th year of Taijian at fifty-three; his son Shubao, the Last Sovereign, succeeded. The histories say: "of great strategy, but of narrow vision." The rise of Chen was Xuan's northern expedition; the fall of Chen was the Lüliang disaster — his game against Qi and Zhou could not match the strength of the north. Eight years after his death, Sui destroyed Chen, and the Southern Dynasties were at an end.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Chenshu*, ch. 5 ("Benji of Emperor Xuan") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 陈后主 · 主要事迹

陈叔宝字元秀，宣帝长子。太建十四年宣帝崩，叔宝即位，改元至德。后主「荒于酒色，不恤政事」：至德年间，大营临春、结绮、望仙三阁，皆以沉檀为饰，金玉珠翠，穷极奢华；宠贵妃张丽华，与江总、孔范等「狎客」游宴赋诗，通宵达旦。其《玉树后庭花》：「丽宇芳林对高阁，新妆艳质本倾城」，遂成「亡国之音」之象征。

祯明三年，隋文帝遣贺若弼、韩擒虎等南下；隋军渡江，陈军望风而溃。韩擒虎自朱雀门入建康，后主与张丽华、孔贵嫔匿于景阳宫井中，为隋军所获——「景阳宫井」，遂为亡国之讥。陈亡，南朝历宋、齐、梁、陈四代一百六十九年而终，天下复归统一。

后主入隋，封长城县公，仁寿四年卒于洛阳，年五十二。史家论后主：「以亡国之君，为艳诗之祖」；其才非不美，然「以风流之资，当板荡之运」，终为亡国所累。陈之亡，非亡于隋之强，而亡于后主之荒淫——「玉树后庭花」一曲，传为千古殷鉴。

> 本地参考：点校本《陈书》卷006《后主纪》、隋书卷002《高祖纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Chen Shubao, styled Yuanxiu, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan. On his father's death in the 14th year of Taijian he took the throne, changing the era to Zhide. The Last Sovereign "drowned in wine and women, and gave no thought to government": in the Zhide years he raised the three pavilions of Linchun, Jieqi, and Wangxian, built of eaglewood and aloes, hung with gold and jade and pearls; he doted on the favorite Zhang Lihua and feasted through the nights with the "companions" Jiang Zong and Kong Fan, writing verse. His *Jade Trees and Rear-Court Flowers* — "bright halls and fragrant woods above the high towers, new gowns and painted faces, the flower of the city" — became the very song of a lost realm.

In the 3rd year of Zhenming, Emperor Wen of Sui sent He Ruobi and Han Qinhu south; the Sui armies crossed the river and the Chen host melted before them. Han Qinhu entered Jiankang by the Vermilion Bird Gate, and the Last Sovereign, with Zhang Lihua and the consort Kong, hid in the well of the Jingyang Palace, where the Sui soldiers drew him up — "the Jingyang well" passing into the mockery of the ages. Chen fell; the Southern Dynasties, Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, one hundred and sixty-nine years, were at an end, and the realm was one again.

Taken into Sui, he was made Duke of Changcheng and died at Luoyang in the 4th year of Renshou, aged fifty-two. The historians say of him: "a lost sovereign and the father of the sensuous verse"; his talent was real, but "with the gifts of a pleasure-lover on the throne of a crumbling age," ruin overtook him. Chen fell not to the strength of Sui but to his own indulgence — the *Jade Trees* remains the eternal warning.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Chenshu*, ch. 6 ("Benji of the Last Sovereign"), and the *Suishu*, ch. 2 ("Benji of Emperor Wen") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 太武帝 · 主要事迹

拓跋焘是北魏第三位皇帝。泰常八年（423）明元帝崩，他即位于平城，明年改元始光；在位二十九年，北魏自此进入扩张高峰。本页以《魏书·世祖纪》为年表主线，灭佛诸事互见《魏书·释老志》。

他的武功是本纪最硬的一条线：始光四年（427）攻取胡夏都城统万，神䴥四年（431）灭赫连夏、取关中，太延二年（436）灭冯氏北燕、辽西归魏，太延五年（439）兵至姑臧、灭沮渠北凉。至此北方统一于北魏，十六国阶段落幕。

武功之外，内政与宗教政策同样醒目。太平真君六年（445）关中盖吴起兵，魏军镇压；而自太平真君五年（444）起，朝廷禁佛毁寺，至七年（446）诏诸州坑沙门，灭佛政策达于高峰。档案将崔浩、寇谦之列为其宗教转向的关联人物，这也是后世评价中争议最集中的一面。

太平真君十一年（450），他大举南征刘宋，兵锋直抵长江北岸的瓜步，与宋文帝隔江对峙，威震江淮而终未能定南。正平二年（452），他在平城为中常侍宗爱所弑，北魏政局随之动荡。

对读线索：与身后的[[n-wei-xiaowen|孝文帝]]对读，可见北魏从铁骑扩张到汉化改制的长线转向；武功极盛与灭佛、被弑的终局并置，正是这位皇帝月旦中性偏负的原因。

bio_parts_en.value:
Tuoba Tao was the third emperor of Northern Wei. In Taichang 8 (423) Emperor Mingyuan died and he ascended the throne at Pingcheng, changing the era name to Shiguang the following year; over twenty-nine years on the throne, Northern Wei entered its peak of expansion. This page takes 《魏书·世祖纪》 as the backbone of its chronology; the persecution of Buddhism is cross-referenced in 《魏书·释老志》.

His martial record is the hardest line in his annals: in Shiguang 4 (427) he captured Tongwan, capital of Hu Xia; in Shenjia 4 (431) he destroyed the Helian Xia and took Guanzhong; in Taiyan 2 (436) he destroyed the Feng family's Northern Yan and western Liaoning fell to Wei; in Taiyan 5 (439) his troops reached Guzang and destroyed the Juqu Northern Liang. With that, the north was unified under Northern Wei, and the Sixteen Kingdoms period came to an end.

Beyond the campaigns, domestic and religious policy were no less striking. In Taiping Zhenjun 6 (445) Ge Wu rose in revolt in Guanzhong and was put down by Wei forces; from Taiping Zhenjun 5 (444) the court banned Buddhism and destroyed temples, and in Zhenjun 7 (446) an edict ordered the provinces to bury monks alive—the persecution reached its peak. The record names Cui Hao and Kou Qianzhi as figures tied to his religious turn, and this remains the most contested side of his later reputation.

In Taiping Zhenjun 11 (450) he launched a massive southern campaign against Liu Song, driving straight to Guabu on the north bank of the Yangzi and facing Emperor Wen of Song across the river—an awesome display that still failed to settle the south. In Zhengping 2 (452) he was murdered at Pingcheng by the palace attendant Zong Ai, and Northern Wei politics fell into turmoil.

A thread for reading across pages: set against his successor

, one sees Northern Wei's long turn from cavalry expansion to sinicizing reform; the juxtaposition of supreme military achievement with the persecution of Buddhism and a murdered emperor's end is exactly why the appraisal of him runs neutral-to-negative.

timeline.title: 即位
timeline.summary: 幼年即位，冯太后临朝，太和改革铺垫。
timeline.summary_en: Ascended the throne as a child; Empress Dowager Feng ruled as regent, laying the groundwork for the Taihe reforms.

timeline.title: 冯太后再临朝
timeline.summary: 文明太后执政高峰，改革铺垫。
timeline.summary_en: Empress Dowager Wenming's rule reached its height, laying the groundwork for reform.

timeline.title: 班禄制
timeline.summary: 班禄酬廉，整顿吏治，太和新政重要一步。
timeline.summary_en: Salaries were granted to reward integrity and discipline the bureaucracy—a key step in the Taihe New Policies.

timeline.title: 均田制
timeline.summary: 颁均田，影响隋唐田制讨论。
timeline.summary_en: The equal-field system was promulgated, deeply shaping later Sui–Tang debates on land tenure.

timeline.title: 三长制
timeline.summary: 立三长，基层组织改革。
timeline.summary_en: The three-elders system was set up, reforming grassroots administration.

timeline.title: 迁都洛阳
timeline.summary: 以南伐为名迁都洛阳，北魏政治中心南移。
timeline.summary_en: Under the pretext of a southern campaign, the capital moved to Luoyang, shifting Northern Wei's political center south.

timeline.title: 禁胡服胡语
timeline.title_en: Ban on Hu Dress and Speech
timeline.summary: 禁鲜卑语、改服饰，推动朝臣汉化。
timeline.summary_en: The Xianbei language was banned and dress reformed, pressing the court toward sinicization.

timeline.title: 定族姓
timeline.summary: 定门阀族姓，士族化。
timeline.summary_en: Aristocratic clan rankings were fixed, hastening the elite's gentrification.

timeline.title: 太子恂废
timeline.summary: 反抗汉化的太子被废，改革代价。
timeline.summary_en: The crown prince, who had resisted sinicization, was deposed—the price of reform.

timeline.title: 改姓元
timeline.summary: 拓跋改姓元，门阀化与汉姓改革。
timeline.summary_en: The Tuoba clan took the Chinese surname Yuan—aristocratization and surname reform combined.

timeline.title: 南伐襄阳线
timeline.summary: 持续南征，消耗国力。
timeline.summary_en: Continuous southern campaigns drained the state's strength.

timeline.title: 南伐崩于军
timeline.summary: 南征途中崩，汉化路线由宣武等延续，亦埋六镇隐患。
timeline.summary_en: He died during a southern campaign; the sinicization line was carried on by Xuanwu and others, while the seeds of the Six Garrisons crisis were also sown.

# 孝文帝 · 主要事迹

元宏（本姓拓跋）是读南北朝史绕不开的改制枢纽。延兴元年（471）幼年即位于平城，前期由文明冯太后临朝主政；本页以《魏书·高祖纪》（卷007上下）为年表主线，辅以《魏书》皇后传、食货志互见与《资治通鉴》对应年段编年对照。

太和年间，班禄制（太和八年）以禄酬廉、整顿吏治，均田制（太和九年）颁行并深远影响隋唐田制讨论，三长制（太和十年）重建基层组织——这套太和新政构成改革的制度骨架。

太和十七年（493）以南伐为名迁都洛阳，北魏政治中心南移；随后禁胡服胡语、定门阀族姓、改拓跋为元姓，汉化全面铺开。改革代价同样清晰：太和二十年（496），反抗汉化的太子元恂被废，宫廷震荡。

晚年持续南伐襄阳一线，消耗国力；太和二十三年（499）崩于南征军中，归葬洛阳。汉化路线由宣武延续，而激进改制与六镇矛盾的争议亦由此埋下。与[[n-wei-taiwu|太武帝]]对读：一先以武功完成北方统一，一以改制重塑王朝面貌——北魏的两副面孔在此分合。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuan Hong (born into the Tuoba clan) is a pivot of institutional reform that no reader of the Northern and Southern Dynasties can bypass. He ascended the throne as a child at Pingcheng in Yanxing 1 (471), with Empress Dowager Wenming (Feng) ruling as regent in his early years. This page takes 《魏书·高祖纪》（卷007上下） as the backbone of its chronology, cross-checked against the empresses' biographies (皇后传) and the Treatise on Food and Money (食货志) in the Book of Wei, and against the corresponding annals of 《资治通鉴》.

During the Taihe era, the salary system (Taihe 8) paid officials to reward integrity and discipline the bureaucracy; the equal-field system (Taihe 9) was promulgated and would deeply shape Sui–Tang debates on land tenure; and the three-elders system (Taihe 10) rebuilt grassroots administration. Together these Taihe New Policies formed the institutional skeleton of the reform.

In Taihe 17 (493), under the pretext of a southern campaign, he moved the capital to Luoyang, shifting Northern Wei's political center south. There followed the ban on Hu dress and speech, the fixing of aristocratic clan rankings, and the change of the Tuoba surname to Yuan—sinicization rolled out in full. The costs were equally clear: in Taihe 20 (496), Crown Prince Yuan Xun, who had resisted sinicization, was deposed, shaking the palace.

In his final years he campaigned persistently on the Xiangyang front, draining the state's strength; in Taihe 23 (499) he died in the army during a southern campaign and was buried back at Luoyang. The sinicization line was carried on by Xuanwu, while the controversies of radical reform and the tensions with the Six Garrisons were sown here as well. Read alongside
: one first completed the unification of the north by arms, the other remade the dynasty's face through institutional reform—the two faces of Northern Wei meet and part in these two men.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉（前赵）高祖 · 主要事迹

刘渊字元海，新兴匈奴人，冒顿之后。幼好学，习《毛诗》《京氏易》及孙吴兵法，「猿臂善射，膂力过人」。八王之乱起，刘渊乘乱于离石起兵，称大单于，旋称汉王，建元元熙——以「汉之甥」自居，尊刘禅为孝怀皇帝，立汉高祖以下三祖五宗神主而祭之，欲争华夏正统。十六国割据，自刘渊始。

永嘉二年，渊即皇帝位，国号汉，迁都平阳，署置百官；遣刘聪、王弥等攻洛阳不克，为日后陷洛之铺垫。然匈奴汉国之制，胡汉分治、军政混行，其政权之根基未固。永嘉四年，刘渊崩，谥光文皇帝。子和继立，旋为弟聪所杀，汉国之政归于刘聪。

刘渊以匈奴之裔，乘晋室之乱而建政权，首开「五胡乱华」之局。其以绍汉为号召、行汉家礼仪，可见汉文化之浸润已深；然其政权终以武功立、以暴政传，后嗣相残、民心不附，不过二十余年而国灭。渊之起兵，非为仁政，实为野心，史家于其「聪敏好学」之外，更见胡汉冲突之始。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷101《刘元海载记》、卷102《刘聪载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。
