bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Yuan, styled Yuanhai, was a Xiongnu of Xinxing, descended from Modu. Studious from youth, he mastered the Mao Odes, the Jing-school Changes, and the military art of Sun and Wu, "long of arm, a fine archer, of unusual strength." When the War of the Eight Princes broke out, he rose at Lishi, styled himself Great Chanyu, then King of Han — claiming descent through a Han princess, he honored Liu Shan as Emperor Xiaohuai and set up the ancestral tablets of the Han emperors to contest legitimacy with the Jin. The Sixteen States era begins with Liu Yuan.

In the 2nd year of Yongjia he took the imperial throne, styled the realm Han, moved his capital to Pingyang, and installed his officials; his lieutenants Liu Cong and Wang Mi attacked Luoyang without success — the prelude to its fall. But the Xiongnu Han state ran on a divided system of Hu and Han, arms and government mixed, and its foundations were never firm. In the 4th year of Yongjia Liu Yuan died, posthumously Guangwen. His son He succeeded and was at once slain by his brother Cong, and the state passed to Cong.

A Xiongnu who rode the Jin collapse to found a state, Liu Yuan opened the "Five Barbarian invasions." His claim of succession to Han and his adoption of Han rites show how deep Chinese culture had sunk into him; yet his state stood on arms and passed on tyranny — heirs murdering heirs, the people's hearts lost — and perished within a generation. His rising was ambition, not benevolence; the historians, beyond his "quickness and love of learning," see the beginning of the Hu–Han conflict.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 101 (records of Liu Yuanhai), ch. 102 (records of Liu Cong) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

names.display_en: Liu Cong, Ancestor Lie of Han (Former Zhao)

emperors.summary: 杀兄和自立，在位八年；永嘉五年陷洛阳俘怀帝，建兴四年陷长安灭西晋，武功极盛；然游猎无度、后宫侈靡，史载记批评之甚。
emperors.summary_en: He slew his brother He to take the throne and reigned eight years; in the 5th year of Yongjia he took Luoyang and captured Emperor Huai, and in the 4th of Jianxing took Chang'an and ended Western Jin — his arms at their height; but his hunting and his harem drew the historians' sharpest censure.

portrait.appearance_basis: 史载无形貌描写。画像宜表现骄盈暴虐的胡族君主之态，衣冠从匈奴汉国制。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 即位
timeline.summary: 杀兄和自立，改元光兴，是为烈宗。
timeline.summary_en: He slew his brother He and took the throne, changing the era to Guangxing.

timeline.title: 陷洛阳
timeline.summary: 刘曜、王弥等破洛阳，俘怀帝，杀王公士民，史称永嘉之乱高峰。
timeline.summary_en: Liu Yao and Wang Mi broke Luoyang, captured Emperor Huai, and slew the princes and people — the summit of the Yongjia disaster.

timeline.title: 杀怀帝于平阳
timeline.summary: 怀帝被俘至平阳，青衣行酒，为聪所杀。
timeline.summary_en: Emperor Huai, brought to Pingyang in captivity, was made to serve wine in servant's dress, then put to death by Cong.

timeline.title: 陷长安灭西晋
timeline.summary: 刘曜破长安，愍帝出降，西晋亡。
timeline.summary_en: Liu Yao took Chang'an, Emperor Min surrendered, and Western Jin was no more.

timeline.title: 刘聪崩
timeline.summary: 崩，子粲继，旋为靳准所杀，政权分裂。
timeline.summary_en: He died; his son Can succeeded and was at once slain by Jin Zhun, and the realm split.

timeline.title: 游猎与后宫
timeline.summary: 史载游猎无度、后宫侈靡，为载记批评焦点。
timeline.summary_en: The records harp on his boundless hunting and his extravagant harem.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉（前赵）烈宗 · 主要事迹

刘聪字载明，刘渊第四子。永嘉四年，杀兄和自立，改元光兴。聪在位八年，武功极盛：永嘉五年，遣刘曜、王弥等破洛阳，俘晋怀帝，杀王公士民三万余人，「永嘉之乱」于此为最；建兴元年，怀帝于平阳青衣行酒，为聪所杀；建兴四年，刘曜破长安，俘愍帝，西晋亡——中国北方，自此尽入胡汉诸国之手。

然刘聪之治，暴虐失德：史载其游猎无度、后宫侈靡，「食则太官，衣则御府」，宠信靳准等佞臣；建兴末又杀愍帝于平阳，弑君之罪，无所忌惮。麟嘉三年，刘聪崩，子粲继，旋为靳准所杀，汉国分裂——刘曜于长安继位改号赵，石勒于襄国称赵王，前赵后赵并立之局始成。

刘聪以灭晋之功，居五胡君主武功之首；然「得天下不以仁义」，其暴政使匈奴汉国仅二世而衰。聪之灭晋，标志五胡十六国之局全面展开：北方自此无复统一，而南朝偏安之局，亦由此定。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷102《刘聪载记》、卷005《怀帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts.value:
刘聪字载明，刘渊第四子。永嘉四年，杀兄和自立，改元光兴。聪在位八年，武功极盛：永嘉五年，遣刘曜、王弥等破洛阳，俘晋怀帝，杀王公士民三万余人，「永嘉之乱」于此为最；建兴元年，怀帝于平阳青衣行酒，为聪所杀；建兴四年，刘曜破长安，俘愍帝，西晋亡——中国北方，自此尽入胡汉诸国之手。

然刘聪之治，暴虐失德：史载其游猎无度、后宫侈靡，「食则太官，衣则御府」，宠信靳准等佞臣；建兴末又杀愍帝于平阳，弑君之罪，无所忌惮。麟嘉三年，刘聪崩，子粲继，旋为靳准所杀，汉国分裂——刘曜于长安继位改号赵，石勒于襄国称赵王，前赵后赵并立之局始成。

刘聪以灭晋之功，居五胡君主武功之首；然「得天下不以仁义」，其暴政使匈奴汉国仅二世而衰。聪之灭晋，标志五胡十六国之局全面展开：北方自此无复统一，而南朝偏安之局，亦由此定。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷102《刘聪载记》、卷005《怀帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Cong, styled Zaiming, was the fourth son of Liu Yuan. In the 4th year of Yongjia he slew his brother He to take the throne, changing the era to Guangxing. His eight years reached the height of arms: in the 5th year of Yongjia he sent Liu Yao and Wang Mi to break Luoyang, capturing Emperor Huai and slaying over thirty thousand princes, officials, and people — the summit of the Yongjia disaster; in the 1st year of Jianxing the captive emperor, made to serve wine in servant's dress, was put to death at Pingyang; in the 4th year of Jianxing Liu Yao took Chang'an and captured Emperor Min — Western Jin was at an end, and the north had passed to the barbarian and half-barbarian states.

His rule was tyranny: the records harp on his boundless hunting and extravagant harem, his favoring of the flatterer Jin Zhun; and he put Emperor Min to death without scruple. In the 3rd year of Linjia he died; his son Can succeeded and was at once slain by Jin Zhun, and the realm split — Liu Yao took the throne at Chang'an and renamed the realm Zhao, while Shi Le styled himself King of Zhao at Xiangguo: the age of Former Zhao and Later Zhao had begun.

For destroying the Jin, Cong stands first in arms among the Five Barbarian sovereigns; but he "won the realm without benevolence," and his tyranny brought the Xiongnu Han state low within two generations. His destruction of Western Jin opened the full age of the Sixteen States: the north would know no unity, and the southern courts' long isolation was fixed.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 102 (records of Liu Cong), ch. 5 ("Benji of Emperor Huai") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 赵（前赵）主 · 主要事迹

刘曜字永明，刘渊族子。靳准之乱后，曜于长安即皇帝位，改国号赵（史称前赵），迁都长安。曜少聪慧，好读书，善属文；在位期间立太学、造浑仪、置史官，关中文化一度振兴。然其亦好杀，史载其「以赤族为戏」，关中氐羌屡叛屡平。

太宁三年，曜与后赵石勒决战洛阳城西。曜饮酒至醉，出阵不利，马陷石渠，为石勒所擒，押送襄国。石勒使曜遗书其子熙，令举国来降，曜不从，遂被杀。翌年，其子熙、胤等退守上邽，为石勒所灭，前赵亡。

刘曜勇武有余，谋略不逮石勒：定都长安而不得关东之助，胡汉离心而民心不附，终以洛阳一败而国亡身死。史家评曰：曜「少聪慧，及长雄武过人」，然「军政失道，民庶流亡」，前赵之亡，实由其失人和之故。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷103《刘曜载记》、卷104《石勒载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Yao, styled Yongming, was a cousin of Liu Yuan's line. After the Jin Zhun troubles he took the imperial throne at Chang'an, renamed the realm Zhao (Former Zhao to history), and made Chang'an his capital. Sharp from youth, fond of books and skilled in prose, he founded an academy, cast an armillary sphere, and appointed historians — Guanzhong's culture revived for a time. But he too loved killing: the records say he "made sport of destroying whole families," and the Di and Qiang of Guanzhong rose and were put down again and again.

In the 3rd year of Taining he met Shi Le of Later Zhao in battle west of Luoyang. Drunk, he rode out at disadvantage, his horse stumbled into a stone ditch, and he was taken and carried to Xiangguo. Shi Le made him write to his son Xi, ordering the realm to surrender; Yao refused, and was put to death. The next year his sons Xi and Yin fell back to Shanggui and were destroyed by Shi Le — Former Zhao was no more.

Yao's courage exceeded his counsel, which fell short of Shi Le's: he fixed his capital at Chang'an without the support of the east, the Hu and the Han were estranged, and the people's hearts were not with him — one defeat at Luoyang ended the state and the man. The historians say he was "sharp from youth and of more than common courage when grown," but "government lost the way and the people scattered": Former Zhao fell for want of men's hearts.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 103 (records of Liu Yao), ch. 104 (records of Shi Le) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后赵高祖 · 主要事迹

石勒是羯人，少时约当西晋永兴前后被掠卖为奴，后来聚众起兵，最终登上帝位——从奴隶到天子的跨度，使他成为十六国史里最戏剧性的创业者。本页以《晋书》卷一百四至一百五石勒载记为年表主线，辅以《资治通鉴》编年（本地参考库已备）。

创业之初，他一度归入刘渊、刘聪的汉赵系统，借汉赵旗帜在华北作战中积累实力。永嘉五年（311）洛阳陷落前后，他参与永嘉之乱后的华北混战，军势迅速坐大，成为割据一方的主力。

太兴二年（319），石勒称赵王、都襄国，正式脱离前赵阴影，后赵政权由此成立；两年后进称大单于，名号与制度同步升格。咸和三年至四年（328–329），他与前赵末主刘曜在洛阳一线决战，破刘曜、灭前赵，北方大部归入后赵版图。咸和五年（330），他在襄国称皇帝，帝制完备，完成了从奴隶到天子的全过程。

石勒并非只有武功。他以张宾为谋主，兴学校、定制度，设君子营安置士人，在胡汉分治的框架下做秩序建设的探索。需要注意，史籍中后赵的残暴记载多须区分石勒本人与其后继者石虎；对石勒本人，史家仍称其雄略。

咸和八年（333），石勒崩于襄国。他生前安排的继承人石弘旋即为石虎所夺，后赵政治迅速恶化，国祚不长。与[[q-qin-fu-jian|前秦苻坚]]对读：同为十六国胡人政权的立国或中兴之主，一前一后，可见那个时代创业与治乱的不同路径。

bio_parts_en.value:
Shi Le was a Jie. In his youth, around the Yongxing era of the Western Jin, he was kidnapped and sold into slavery; he later gathered a following, rose in arms, and finally ascended the imperial throne — the span from slave to Son of Heaven makes him the most dramatic state-founder in the history of the Sixteen Kingdoms. This page takes the Shi Le annals in juan 104–105 of the 《晋书》 as its chronological backbone, supplemented by the chronicle of the 《资治通鉴》 (available in the local reference library).

At the start of his enterprise he attached himself for a time to the Han-Zhao system of Liu Yuan and Liu Cong, building strength through campaigns in north China under the Han-Zhao banner. Around the fall of Luoyang in Yongjia 5 (311), he joined the melee that followed the Yongjia upheaval in north China; his military power swelled rapidly, making him a leading force among the regional powers.

In Taixing 2 (319) Shi Le took the title King of Zhao and made Xiangguo his capital, formally stepping out of Former Zhao's shadow — the Later Zhao regime was thereby founded; two years later he advanced to Great Chanyu, his titles and institutions rising in step. In Xianhe 3–4 (328–329) he fought the decisive battle along the Luoyang line against Liu Yao, the last ruler of Former Zhao: he defeated Liu Yao, destroyed Former Zhao, and most of the north entered the Later Zhao map. In Xianhe 5 (330) he proclaimed himself emperor at Xiangguo, completing the imperial system — and with it the entire passage from slave to Son of Heaven.

Shi Le was not a man of martial feats alone. He made Zhang Bin his chief strategist, promoted schools and fixed institutions, established the Gentlemen's Camp to house men of letters, and explored the building of order within the framework of Hu-Han dual rule. One caveat: the records of Later Zhao cruelty in the histories must often be divided between Shi Le himself and his successor Shi Hu; of Shi Le himself, historians still speak of his boldness of design.

In Xianhe 8 (333) Shi Le died at Xiangguo. Shi Hong, the heir he had arranged, was at once dispossessed by Shi Hu; Later Zhao politics deteriorated quickly, and the dynastic line did not last long. Read him against
: both were founders or restorers of Hu states in the Sixteen Kingdoms period, one earlier and one later, and together they show the era's different paths of state-building and of order and collapse.

# 后赵武帝 · 主要事迹

石虎字季龙，石勒之侄。骁勇善战，为石勒方面大将，攻城略地，多出其力。咸和八年石勒崩，虎受遗辅石弘，旋专权；咸和九年，废杀石弘自立，称居摄赵天王，后称帝。石虎迁都于邺，大营宫殿苑囿，「发民夫四十余万」筑华林苑、猎场，又括民女充后宫，史称百姓愁怨。

石虎之暴，为十六国君主之最：役民无度，杀人如麻，「既而自以无子，复立其幼子」，诸子争立，骨肉相残；又发兵攻前燕、前凉，武功虽盛，而民力已竭。永和五年，石虎崩，诸子为争帝位自相残杀，石闵（冉闵）乘乱起兵，杀胡人二十余万，后赵迅即崩溃——其盛也暴，其亡也速。

史家论石虎：「季龙以凶戾之资，奋残暴之性，虽复冠带蛮貊，终为豺狼之德。」后赵之武功，尽丧于暴政；其「胡汉相杀」之祸，更为五胡之乱中最惨烈者。虎之兴亡，足为暴政亡国之鉴。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷106《石季龙载记》、卷107《石闵载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Shi Hu, styled Jilong, was the nephew of Shi Le, a fierce warrior who took cities for his uncle as one of his field commanders. In the 8th year of Xianhe Le died; Hu, by the late will, assisted Shi Hong — and at once seized power. In the 9th year he deposed and slew Hong and stood himself, calling himself Heavenly King of Zhao Regent, later emperor. He moved the capital to Ye, raised palaces and parks on a grand scale, and "drove over 400,000 laborers" to build the Huayuan park and hunting grounds; he swept the realm's women into his harem — the records say the people grieved and raged.

His tyranny was the worst of the Sixteen States: corvée without limit, slaughter without mercy; and with his sons contending, kin slew kin. He campaigned against Former Yan and Former Liang, his arms at their height while the people's strength ran out. In the 5th year of Yonghe he died; his sons fought for the throne, and Shi Min (Ran Min) rose in the chaos and slew over 200,000 Hu — Later Zhao collapsed at once. It rose in tyranny and fell in a moment.

The historians say of him: "With a savage nature and a brutal temper, though he put on the robes of civilization, his virtue was the wolf's." The realm's strength was spent in cruelty; and the Hu–Han slaughter of his fall was the bitterest of the barbarian age. His rise and ruin stand as the warning of tyranny.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 106 (records of Shi Jilong), ch. 107 (records of Shi Min) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 成汉太宗 · 主要事迹

李雄字仲俊，巴氐流民首领李特之子。太安二年，李特与益州刺史罗尚相攻，兵败被杀；雄继统部众，与罗尚等相持。建兴元年，雄称成都王，建元；晏平元年，即皇帝位，国号大成，都成都。成汉遂与中原诸国并立，为十六国中偏安巴蜀者。

李雄在位三十年，史称其「宽政安蜀」：轻徭薄赋，刑狱宽简，「赋役俱省，民庶丰溢」，蜀人安之。雄无子，养兄李荡之子班为太子；玉衡二十四年，雄崩，兄子班继位。然李雄诸子不服，李期等发动政变杀班自立，成汉自此中衰——雄之宽政，未能传之后嗣。

史家评李雄：「雄以宽仁之量，抚流移之民，故能据有巴蜀，垂三十年。」在十六国暴君辈出之际，李雄之治实属难得；然传位不明、诸子争立，其宽政终成昙花一现。成汉后为东晋桓温所灭，偏安之局遂终。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷121《李雄载记》、卷120《李特载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Xiong, styled Zhongjun, was the son of Li Te, leader of the Ba-Di refugee host. In the 2nd year of Tai'an, Li Te, fighting the Yi Province governor Luo Shang, was defeated and slain; Xiong took command and held off Luo Shang. In the 1st year of Jianxing he styled himself King of Chengdu and opened an era; in the 1st year of Yanping he took the imperial throne, styling the realm Dacheng with its capital at Chengdu. Cheng Han stood beside the states of the Central Plains — the one of the Sixteen that held Bashu alone.

In thirty years Xiong's rule was the most benign of the age: light levies, easy justice, "tax and corvée both spared, the people prosperous," and the people of Shu at peace. He had no son and raised his nephew Ban as heir; when he died in the 24th year of Yuheng and Ban succeeded, Xiong's own sons would not bear it — Li Qi and the others murdered Ban, and Cheng Han began its decline. His benevolence could not bequeath itself.

The historians say: "With a measure of benevolence Xiong nourished the refugees, and so held Bashu for nearly thirty years." Amid the tyrants of the Sixteen States his rule stands out; but the succession was unsecured and his sons tore the state — the good rule was a brief spring. Huan Wen of Eastern Jin later destroyed Cheng Han, and the enclave ended.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 121 (records of Li Xiong), ch. 120 (records of Li Te) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 前燕文明帝 · 主要事迹

慕容皝字元真，鲜卑慕容部首领慕容廆之子。咸和八年廆死，皝嗣辽东公，讨平其兄翰等之乱；咸康三年，自称燕王——前燕王政自此始。皝建元、置僚属，筑龙城而都之，开拓辽西；又破宇文部、击段部，辽东霸权遂固。

皝之治，兼用胡汉：以汉族士人裴嶷、封奕等为谋主，劝农桑、立学校，「览政之暇，亲临东庠考试学生」；军事上则倚其弟慕容翰、慕容恪等名将。慕容部之崛起，自皝而兴。永和四年，皝崩，谥文明皇帝，子儁继位。

慕容皝以辽东一隅，经营前燕基业，「威德兼举，士庶归心」；其子慕容儁灭冉魏、入中原，其孙慕容暐时前燕全盛——皆皝奠基之功。然皝猜忌兄弟，逼走慕容翰，晚年兄弟相攻之祸已伏；燕之兴也勃，其亡也忽，内乱之根，盖植于此。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷109《慕容皝载记》、卷110《慕容儁载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Murong Huang, styled Yuanzhen, was the son of Murong Hui, chief of the Murong Xianbei. In the 8th year of Xianhe Hui died; Huang succeeded as Duke of Liaodong and put down the rising of his brothers; in the 3rd year of Xiankang he styled himself King of Yan — the kingship of Former Yan began. He opened an era, installed officers, built Longcheng as his capital, opened up Liaoxi, broke the Yuwen tribe and struck the Duan, and his hegemony of Liaodong was fixed.

He ruled with both Hu and Han: the Han gentry Pei Ni, Feng Yi, and the rest were his counselors; he encouraged farming and mulberries, founded schools, and "in his leisure from government examined the students in person"; in arms he leaned on his brothers Murong Han and Murong Ke, generals of the first rank. The rise of the Murong house began with Huang. He died in the 4th year of Yonghe, posthumously Emperor Wenming, and his son Jun succeeded.

From one corner of Liaodong Huang built the foundations of Former Yan, "his authority and virtue together drawing the gentry and the people." His son Jun destroyed Ran Wei and entered the Central Plains; his grandson Wei reigned at the height of Former Yan — the work of Huang's founding. But he distrusted his brothers, driving Murong Han away, and the seed of the house's internal wars was sown here: Former Yan rose swiftly and fell swiftly, and the root of the ruin lay in the founder.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 109 (records of Murong Huang), ch. 110 (records of Murong Jun) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 前燕景昭帝 · 主要事迹

慕容儁字宣英，慕容皝次子。永和四年皝崩，儁嗣燕王。永和六年，乘后赵石虎之死、中原大乱，儁遣慕容恪、慕容评等南下争河北，取蓟城、克中山；永和八年，俘杀冉闵，遂即皇帝位，国号燕——前燕入主中原，与东晋、前秦鼎足而三。

儁迁都邺，据石氏故都，「宫室制度，皆仿洛阳」；又令州郡核实户口，劝课农桑。前燕全盛时，「南至汝颍，东尽青齐，西抵崤渑」，为十六国中之强者。然儁在位后期，好大喜功：欲发兵百万攻东晋、前秦，与东晋争正统；又猜忌其弟慕容垂。光寿四年，儁崩，子暐年仅十一继位，慕容恪辅政。

慕容儁以灭冉魏之功入主中原，前燕之盛极于此；然其穷兵黩武、猜忌宗室，为前燕中衰埋下伏线。史家评曰：儁「雄毅多权略」，然「以武立国，不修文德」，其兴也勃焉，其亡也忽焉。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷110《慕容儁载记》、卷111《慕容暐载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

儁迁都邺，据石氏故都，「宫室制度，皆仿洛阳」；又令州郡核实户口，劝课农桑。前燕全盛时，「南至汝颍，东尽青齐，西抵崤渑」，为十六国中之强者。然儁在位后期，好大喜功：欲发兵百万攻东晋、前秦，与东晋争正统；又猜忌其弟慕容垂。光寿四年，儁崩，子暐年仅十一继位，慕容恪辅政。

慕容儁以灭冉魏之功入主中原，前燕之盛极于此；然其穷兵黩武、猜忌宗室，为前燕中衰埋下伏线。史家评曰：儁「雄毅多权略」，然「以武立国，不修文德」，其兴也勃焉，其亡也忽焉。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷110《慕容儁载记》、卷111《慕容暐载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Murong Jun, styled Xuan Ying, was the second son of Murong Huang. On his father's death in the 4th year of Yonghe he succeeded as King of Yan. In the 6th year, riding the chaos after Shi Hu's death, he sent Murong Ke, Murong Ping, and the others south into Hebei, taking Ji and Zhongshan; in the 8th year he captured and slew Ran Min and took the imperial throne, styling the realm Yan — Former Yan entered the Central Plains, standing with Eastern Jin and Former Qin as the third of the age.

He moved the capital to Ye, the old seat of the Shi house, "his palaces and institutions modeled on Luoyang," and ordered the provinces to verify the household registers and encourage farming. At its height Former Yan "reached the Ru and Ying in the south, Qing and Qi in the east, and the Xiao and Mian in the west" — among the strongest of the Sixteen States. But in his later years he grew vainglorious: he would raise a million men against Jin and Qin to contest legitimacy, and he distrusted his brother Murong Chui. He died in the 4th year of Guangshou; his son Wei, eleven, succeeded under Murong Ke's regency.

For destroying Ran Wei and entering the Central Plains, Jun brought Former Yan to its height; but his endless wars and his suspicion of his own kin laid the fuse of its decline. The historians say he was "bold and full of stratagems," yet "a realm won by arms, not adorned by virtue — it rose swiftly and fell swiftly."

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 110 (records of Murong Jun), ch. 111 (records of Murong Wei) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 前秦高祖 · 主要事迹

苻健字建业，略阳氐人，苻洪第三子。苻洪为后赵所害，健统其众。永和六年，健率众自枋头入关，击破杜洪，据长安；皇始元年，自称天王、大单于，国号大秦，都长安；皇始二年，即皇帝位。前秦立国之基，自苻健始。

皇始中，东晋桓温北伐，入关至霸上，关中震恐。苻健坚壁清野，尽收其麦，温军粮尽而退——「健以逸待劳」，遂保关中。苻健在位五年，抚流民、劝农桑、置百官，「虽戎狄之俗，渐染华风」。皇始五年，健崩，谥景明皇帝。其子苻生继位，残暴无道，旋为侄苻坚所杀——前秦之大业，终落于苻坚之手。

苻健以氐族之身，乘乱据关中，为前秦开创基业；其拒桓温之役，尤见将略。然健虽开基，未及大治，子生之暴、侄坚之兴，皆其身后之事。前秦自苻坚始成为十六国最强者，然其根柢，实植于苻健之世。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷112《苻健载记》、卷113《苻坚载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Fu Jian, styled Jianye, was a Di of Lüeyang, third son of Fu Hong. When Fu Hong was done to death by Later Zhao, Jian took command of his host. In the 6th year of Yonghe he led his men through the pass, broke Du Hong, and took Chang'an; in the 1st year of Huangshi he styled himself Heavenly King and Great Chanyu of the realm Great Qin with his capital at Chang'an; in the 2nd year he took the imperial throne. The foundations of Former Qin were laid by Jian.

In mid-Huangshi, Huan Wen of Eastern Jin campaigned north and entered the pass, reaching Bashan, and Guanzhong was shaken. Jian cleared the land of its grain and held his walls; Wen's army ran out of food and withdrew — "Jian, at ease, wore the invader out," and Guanzhong was saved. In five years he gathered the refugees, encouraged farming, and installed his officials, "the barbarian custom gradually taking on Chinese ways." He died in the 5th year of Huangshi, posthumously Emperor Jingming. His son Sheng succeeded, a cruel tyrant, and was soon slain by his nephew Fu Jian — the great enterprise of Former Qin passed to the nephew.

A Di who seized Guanzhong in the chaos and founded Former Qin, Jian showed real generalship in denying Huan Wen. He founded the state but did not live to perfect it; the tyrant Sheng and the rise of Fu Jian were the work of his successors. Former Qin became the strongest of the Sixteen States under Fu Jian — but its roots were planted in Jian's reign.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 112 (records of Fu Jian), ch. 113 (records of Fu Jian the Great Ancestor) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 前秦世祖 · 主要事迹

苻坚（357—385 在位）是十六国时期最接近统一天下的前秦君主。永兴元年（357）他诛暴主苻生，即天王位，改元永兴，前秦由此进入苻坚时代。本页以《晋书·苻坚载记》（卷113–114）为年表主线，辅以《资治通鉴·晋纪》编年对照。

即位之后，他把国政委于王猛。王猛整肃吏治、打击贵戚，前秦国力急升，构成苻坚一朝的文治底色。武功随之而起：太和五年（370）王猛克邺，前燕遂灭，北方统一进程加速；太元元年（376）再灭前凉，兼及代地，河西归于前秦，北方大体统一，版图臻于巅峰。

巅峰之后是急转。太元七年（382）朝议伐晋，其时王猛已卒，谏阻无力；次年苻坚决意南伐，史载有「投鞭于江，足断其流」一类豪语，倾国出兵。太元八年（383）淝水一战大败于东晋谢安、谢玄一系，前秦由此崩解，各族复起。需要说明的是，「投鞭断流」语出记载的文学性颇浓，但南伐的战略责任归于苻坚本人，这一点仍成立。

太元九年（384）慕容垂独立，燕秦瓦解；次年苻坚西奔五将山一带，为姚苌所害，前秦迅速瓦解。读苻坚，可与[[n-wei-taiwu|太武帝]]对读：两者皆以武力整合北方，一败于南征而国解，一再合北方而开启北朝，可见十六国北朝兴亡的节奏。

bio_parts_en.value:
Fu Jian (r. 357–385) was the Former Qin ruler who came closest to unifying all under Heaven in the Sixteen Kingdoms period. In Yongxing 1 (357) he executed the tyrannical ruler Fu Sheng, took the title Heavenly King, and changed the era name to Yongxing; Former Qin thereby entered the age of Fu Jian. This page takes the 《晋书·苻坚载记》 (juan 113–114) as its chronological backbone, checked against the chronicle of the 《资治通鉴·晋纪》.

After his enthronement he entrusted the affairs of state to Wang Meng. Wang Meng disciplined the bureaucracy and struck at powerful kinsmen; Former Qin's strength surged, forming the civil-government foundation of Fu Jian's reign. Military achievement followed: in Taihe 5 (370) Wang Meng took Ye, Former Yan was destroyed, and the unification of the north accelerated; in Taiyuan 1 (376) he further destroyed Former Liang, reaching as far as the land of Dai; Hexi fell to Former Qin, the north was largely unified, and the map reached its peak.

After the peak came the sharp turn. In Taiyuan 7 (382) the court debated attacking Jin; Wang Meng was already dead, and remonstrance carried no force. The next year Fu Jian resolved on the southern campaign — the histories record boasts of the sort "throw our whips into the river and they would dam its flow" — and mobilized the entire state. In Taiyuan 8 (383), at the single battle of the Fei River, he was crushingly defeated by the Eastern Jin line of Xie An and Xie Xuan; Former Qin disintegrated and the various peoples rose again. It should be noted that the phrase "whips damming the river" carries a strong literary coloring in the sources, but strategic responsibility for the southern campaign rests with Fu Jian himself — that point still stands.

In Taiyuan 9 (384) Murong Chui declared independence and the Yan-Qin order collapsed; the next year Fu Jian fled west to the Wujiangshan area, where he was killed by Yao Chang, and Former Qin rapidly fell apart. Reading Fu Jian, one may set him against

: both integrated the north by force; one broke on a southern campaign and lost his state, the other re-unified the north and opened the Northern Dynasties — together they show the rhythm of rise and fall across the Sixteen Kingdoms and Northern Dynasties.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后秦太祖 · 主要事迹

姚苌字景茂，南安赤亭羌人，姚弋仲第二十四子。淝水之战后，前秦土崩，姚苌于白雀元年叛苻坚自立，称万年秦王于北地——后秦始。白雀二年，姚苌围新平，苻坚走五将山，为苌所擒，缢杀之——一代雄主苻坚，竟死于其臣之刃。

建初元年，姚苌即皇帝位于长安，国号大秦。后秦立国之初，关中群雄并起：苻登据陇东，与前秦残部相攻，姚苌与苻登战于安定、新平间，久而不决；又讨平关中各郡。建初八年，姚苌病笃，苻登攻之益急，苌欲遁，为众所止，卒于长安，谥武昭皇帝。

姚苌以羌族之身，乘乱而起，弑苻坚而开基立国，史家谓之「枭雄」；然其弑主之罪、猜忌之性，使其形象在十六国君主中尤为负面。后秦之兴，兴于姚苌之谋；后秦之德，失于姚苌之弑——其子姚兴崇文兴佛，庶几补救，然终不能洗其父之污名。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yao Chang, styled Jingmao, was a Qiang of Chiting in Nan'an, twenty-fourth son of Yao Yizhong. After the Fei River defeat, as Former Qin crumbled, Chang turned against Fu Jian in the 1st year of Baique and styled himself King of Wannian Qin in Beidi — the beginning of Later Qin. In the 2nd year of Baique he besieged Xinping; Fu Jian, fled to Mount Wujiang, was seized and strangled — the great hero of Former Qin died by his own minister's hand.

In the 1st year of Jianchu Chang took the imperial throne at Chang'an, styling the realm Great Qin. The founding years were hard: Fu Deng held the Longdong with the remnants of Former Qin, and Chang fought him between Anding and Xinping for years without decision; the commanderies of Guanzhong rose and were put down. In the 8th year of Jianchu, gravely ill with Fu Deng pressing, he wished to flee; his men would not let him, and he died at Chang'an, posthumously Emperor Wuzhao.

A Qiang who rose with the times, slew Fu Jian, and founded a realm — the historians call him an adventurer; his slaying of his lord and his jealousy blacken his name among the Sixteen States' sovereigns. Later Qin rose by Chang's cunning and lost its virtue by his crime; his son Yao Xing's patronage of learning and Buddhism partly repaired the name, but could not wash it clean.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 116 (records of Yao Chang), ch. 114 (records of Fu Jian) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 后秦高祖 · 主要事迹

姚兴字子略，姚苌长子。建初八年苌崩，兴即位于长安。姚兴在位二十二年，为后秦全盛之期：皇初年间，兴破苻登，灭前秦残部，基本统一关陇——「陇右休屠、匈奴等皆降附」；又取洛阳，据有河东。后秦疆域，西至河西，东达洛阳，为十六国后期之强者。

姚兴之治，崇文尚佛：弘始三年，迎鸠摩罗什入长安，译经讲法，僧徒云集，「远近诸方，莫不归仰」，长安遂为佛教译经中心；又立律学于长安，召郡国生徒数百人受业，考其优劣；听政之暇，亲讲佛经。姚兴之世，后秦文化之盛，为十六国所仅见。

然姚兴晚年，立嗣不明：太子泓与弟弼相争，兴「以药疾」，诸子相攻，后秦元气大伤。永和元年，姚兴崩；永和十三年，后秦为东晋刘裕所灭。史家评姚兴：「留心政事，包容荒诞，虽政刑未理，而风教可观。」其文治在十六国君主中首屈一指，惜其武功不逮前代。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷117《姚兴载记》、卷118《姚泓载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yao Xing, styled Zilue, was the eldest son of Yao Chang. On his father's death in the 8th year of Jianchu he took the throne at Chang'an. His twenty-two years were the height of Later Qin: in the early Huangchu years he broke Fu Deng, destroyed the remnants of Former Qin, and roughly united Guanzhong and Longxi — "the Xiongnu of the Longyou submitted" — and he took Luoyang and held Hedong. The realm stretched from Hexi in the west to Luoyang in the east, one of the strong states of the later Sixteen.

His rule favored letters and Buddhism: in the 3rd year of Hongshi he brought Kumarajiva to Chang'an, where the master translated the scriptures before throngs of monks — "all quarters looked up to him" — and Chang'an became the center of scripture translation; he founded a law academy, summoned hundreds of students from the provinces to study and examined their merits; in his leisure from government he lectured on the sutras himself. The culture of his court was unique among the Sixteen States.

But his succession was ill-managed: the heir Hong and his brother Bi contended, and while Xing lay ill his sons fought, and the state's strength ebbed. He died in the 1st year of Yonghe; in the 13th, Liu Yu of Eastern Jin destroyed Later Qin. The historians credit him with "care for government" and note "though law and punishment were imperfect, manners and teaching were admirable": in civil rule he stands first among the Sixteen States' sovereigns, but in arms he fell short of his father.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 117 (records of Yao Xing), ch. 118 (records of Yao Hong) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 后燕成武帝 · 主要事迹

慕容垂字道明，慕容皝第五子。十三岁随父征伐，「勇冠三军」，为前燕名将；枋头之战，大破桓温，威震中原。然为慕容评所忌，前燕亡后奔秦，仕苻坚。淝水之战，垂军独全，坚败后护之还洛阳——然其异志已萌。

燕元元年，垂叛秦，称燕王于荥阳，后燕始。建兴元年，即皇帝位于中山。垂复国后，先后讨平翟魏、西燕，又大破东晋桓冲；建兴十年，太子宝伐北魏，大败于参合陂，死者数万——垂之霸业，于此受挫。建兴十一年，垂亲征北魏，欲报参合陂之仇，行至上谷祖阳，病笃而崩，年七十一。

慕容垂一生，为将则名冠当世，为君则开国复燕；然「参合陂之败，虽非亲征，实丧其锐」——垂之死，后燕中衰，数年后即为北魏所灭。史家评垂：「少岐嶷有器度，身长七尺七寸，手垂过膝」，然「仁而不武，未能剪灭群雄」；其以旧将复国，终因后嗣不肖、强敌环伺而功败垂成。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷123《慕容垂载记》、卷124《慕容宝载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Murong Chui, styled Daoming, was the fifth son of Murong Huang. He followed his father's campaigns from thirteen, "first in valor of the whole army," the great general of Former Yan; at Fangtou he shattered Huan Wen, and his name ran through the Central Plains. But Murong Ping's jealousy drove him out; when Former Yan fell he took refuge with Fu Jian of Qin. At the Fei River, his was the one army left whole; he escorted the defeated Fu Jian back to Luoyang — but his designs were already formed.

In the 1st year of Yanyuan he turned on Qin, styled himself King of Yan at Xingyang, and Later Yan began. In the 1st year of Jianxing he took the imperial throne at Zhongshan. His restoration swept away the Zhai-Wei and Western Yan, and he broke Huan Chong of Eastern Jin; in the 10th year of Jianxing his heir Bao campaigned against Northern Wei and was shattered at the Canhe marshes, tens of thousands dead — the hinge of his fortunes. In the 11th year, campaigning in person to avenge the marshes, he fell ill at Zuyang in Shanggu and died, aged seventy-one.

As a general he was without equal in his age; as a sovereign he restored the Yan line. But "the Canhe disaster, though not his own campaign, broke his edge" — with his death Later Yan declined, and within years Wei destroyed it. The historians say he was "marked from youth for greatness, seven feet seven tall, his hands hanging past his knees," yet "benevolent without being martial, unable to cut down the heroes of the age": a veteran who rebuilt a state, only to see his heirs and his enemies undo it.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 123 (records of Murong Chui), ch. 124 (records of Murong Bao) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 西秦烈祖 · 主要事迹

乞伏国仁，陇西鲜卑乞伏部首领。淝水之战后，前秦瓦解，国仁于建义元年据苑川，称大单于，西秦始。国仁在位四年，讨破邻近鲜卑诸部如鲜卑匹兰、密贵等，拓地至金城；又与关陇诸政权周旋，受前秦苻登之官爵，为苑川王。

建义四年，国仁崩，其弟乾归继位，西秦延续。乾归时西秦略有规模，然其地狭力弱，与后秦、南凉、北凉相攻伐；西秦虽历国仁、乾归、炽磐三代，始终局促于陇西一隅，后为夏国所灭。

史家评国仁：草创开国，享国短促。西秦在十六国中为最弱小者之一，其兴也倚于前秦之崩，其亡也因于群雄之逼；乞伏氏以陇西鲜卑之部，割据数十年，可谓乱世自存之难。国仁之名，不过十六国风云中之一瞬。

bio_parts_en.value:
Qifu Guoren was the chief of the Qifu Xianbei of Longxi. After the Fei River defeat, with Former Qin dissolving, he held Yuanchuan in the 1st year of Jianyi and styled himself Great Chanyu — the beginning of Western Qin. In his four years he broke the neighboring Xianbei tribes, the Pilan and the Migu and the rest, extending his lands to Jincheng; he dealt with the powers of Guanzhong and Longxi, accepting from Fu Deng the titles of King of Yuanchuan and more.

He died in the 4th year of Jianyi, his brother Gangui carrying on Western Qin. Under Gangui and then Qifu Chipan the state had some measure of size, but it was ever cramped in one corner of Longxi, fighting Later Qin, Southern Liang, and Northern Liang, and was finally destroyed by the Xia state.

The historians judge him: a rough founding, and the realm's years were few. Western Qin was among the weakest of the Sixteen States; it rose on Former Qin's ruin and fell before the stronger powers — the difficulty of a single Xianbei tribe holding its own through decades of chaos. Guoren's name is but a moment in the storm.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 125 (records of Qifu Guoren), ch. 125 (records of Qifu Gangui) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后凉懿武帝 · 主要事迹

吕光字世明，略阳氐人，苻坚大将。建元十九年，奉苻坚命征西域：率步骑七万，越流沙，破焉耆、龟兹，「诸国皆降」，得鸠摩罗什以归。太安元年，光东还，闻苻坚为姚苌所杀，遂据姑臧自立，称凉州牧；龙飞元年，称三河王，后称天王——后凉始立。

吕光以武功据河西，然其治国无方：任子为将，诸子相攻；猜忌宗室，杀戮无辜。其晚年，秃发乌孤、沮渠蒙逊、段业等相继叛之，后凉之地四分五裂。承康元年，吕光崩，诸子争立，后凉遂衰，数年后为后秦所灭。

史家评吕光：「少沈毅，有器度」，然「性多猜忌，不任其下」。吕光以西征之功、据凉州之地，本可成一方之业；然其以武夫之资治国，无怀柔之量，河西诸部离心，终致后凉速亡。其征西域之功，为十六国君主所仅见，然武功之盛，不救治国之败。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷122《吕光载记》、卷125《秃发乌孤载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Lü Guang, styled Shiming, was a Di of Lüeyang and a general of Fu Jian. In the 19th year of Jianyuan, by Fu Jian's order, he campaigned in the Western Regions: with seventy thousand horse and foot he crossed the drifting sands, broke Karashahr and Kucha, "the kingdoms all submitting," and brought back Kumarajiva. In the 1st year of Tai'an, returning east on word that Yao Chang had slain Fu Jian, he held Guzang and stood alone, styling himself Governor of Liangzhou; in the 1st year of Longfei he took the title King of the Three Rivers, later Heavenly King — the beginning of Later Liang.

Guanzheng he was strong; governing he was without art: he made generals of his sons, and the sons fought; he distrusted his kin and slew them. In his old age Tufa Wugu, Juqu Mengxun, Duan Ye, and the others rose against him one after another, and his realm was torn into four. He died in the 1st year of Chengkang; his sons contended, Later Liang decayed, and within years Later Qin took it.

The historians say he was "resolute from youth and of real bearing," yet "jealous by nature, untrusting of his subordinates." With the glory of the western campaign and the possession of Liangzhou he might have built a lasting state; but he ruled as a soldier, without the arts of conciliation, the peoples of Hexi fell away, and Later Liang passed swiftly. His western conquest stands alone among the Sixteen States' sovereigns; but the glory of arms did not cure the failure of government.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 122 (records of Lü Guang), ch. 125 (records of Tufa Wugu) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 南凉武王 · 主要事迹

秃发乌孤，河西鲜卑秃发部首领。太初元年，叛后凉吕光，自称西平王，筑廉川堡为都，据湟中——南凉始。乌孤「雄勇有大志」，太初二年，拓地至广武、湟河，改称武威王；又用汉族士人史嵩等，谋据河西。

太初三年，乌孤酒醉，坠马伤胁，寻崩，年约四十。其弟利鹿孤、傉檀相继继位，南凉时盛时衰：利鹿孤徙都西平，傉檀徙都乐都，与后秦、北凉、西秦相攻伐。然南凉地狭民寡，终为西秦所灭。

史家评乌孤：「草创南凉，享国不永。」乌孤以河西鲜卑之部，乘后凉之衰而自立，其兴也速；然其酒祸丧身，后嗣之业不昌。秃发与拓跋同源之传说，见载记之序——其族之命运，竟与拓跋氏一盛一衰，相映成趣。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷126《秃发乌孤载记》、卷126《秃发傉檀载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Tufa Wugu was the chief of the Tufa Xianbei of Hexi. In the 1st year of Taichu he turned against Lü Guang of Later Liang, styled himself King of Xiping, and built the fort of Lianchuan as his capital, holding the Huangzhong — the beginning of Southern Liang. "Bold and great of purpose," he extended his lands to Guangwu and Huanghe in the 2nd year and took the title King of Wuwei; he drew in the Han gentry, Shi Song and the rest, and planned to hold Hexi.

In the 3rd year of Taichu, drunk, he fell from his horse, hurt his ribs, and died, around forty. His brothers Lilugu and then Nutan succeeded, and Southern Liang rose and fell by turns — Lilugu moving the capital to Xiping, Nutan to Ledu, fighting Later Qin, Northern Liang, and Western Qin. Cramped and poor in men, it was finally destroyed by Western Qin.

The historians judge Wugu: "a rough founding of Southern Liang, and the realm's years were few." A Hexi Xianbei tribe seizing its chance on Later Liang's decline, it rose swiftly; his death by drink left the succession weak. The records' preface notes the legend that the Tufa and the Tuoba share a common origin — the fate of the one house rising while the other fell is a mirror of the age.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 126 (records of Tufa Wugu), ch. 126 (records of Tufa Nutan) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 北凉武宣王 · 主要事迹

沮渠蒙逊，临松卢水胡人，「博涉群史，颇晓天文」。龙飞二年，与兄男成等拥立段业为凉州牧，反后凉；永安元年，蒙逊杀段业自立，称凉州牧、张掖公——北凉实始。蒙逊旋迁都姑臧，称河西王，据有河西走廊之大部分。

蒙逊之业，以灭西凉为高峰：玄始十年，率军破敦煌，西凉李歆战死，李氏西凉亡，河西遂为一统。北凉全盛时，「东据金城，西控敦煌」，与北魏、南朝宋通使往来，又迎昙无谶译经，佛教大兴。义和三年，蒙逊崩，其子牧犍继位；承平七年，北魏太武帝亲征，牧犍出降，北凉亡——五凉之局，至此而终。

史家评蒙逊：「性雄杰，有勇略，善权变。」其以胡人之身，弑主自立，权变有余而信义不足；然其经营河西三十余年，保境安民、兴文倡佛，为五凉诸国中命祚最长者。北凉之亡，亦标志五胡十六国之局渐入尾声。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷129《沮渠蒙逊载记》、卷099《沮渠牧犍传》及《魏书·沮渠蒙逊传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

史家评蒙逊：「性雄杰，有勇略，善权变。」其以胡人之身，弑主自立，权变有余而信义不足；然其经营河西三十余年，保境安民、兴文倡佛，为五凉诸国中命祚最长者。北凉之亡，亦标志五胡十六国之局渐入尾声。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷129《沮渠蒙逊载记》、卷099《沮渠牧犍传》及《魏书·沮渠蒙逊传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Juqu Mengxun was a Lushui Hu of Linsong, "learned in the histories and versed in astronomy." In the 2nd year of Longfei, with his brother Nancheng, he pushed Duan Ye to the governorship of Liangzhou against Later Liang; in the 1st year of Yong'an he slew Duan Ye and stood himself, styling himself Governor of Liangzhou and Duke of Zhangye — the real beginning of Northern Liang. He moved the capital to Guzang, took the title King of Hexi, and held most of the Hexi corridor.

His crowning deed was the destruction of Western Liang: in the 10th year of Xuanshi he broke Dunhuang, Li Xin fell in battle, and the Li house's Western Liang perished — Hexi was one. At its height Northern Liang "held Jincheng in the east and Dunhuang in the west," sent envoys to Northern Wei and to the Song court of the south, and welcomed the translator Tan Wuchen, so that Buddhism flourished. He died in the 3rd year of Yihe; his son Mujian succeeded, and in the 7th year of Chengping Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei campaigned in person, Mujian surrendered, and Northern Liang was no more — the five Liangs ended.

The historians say of him: "bold of nature, of real courage, skilled in shifts." A Hu who slew his lord to take power, he had cunning in plenty and faith in little; yet he held Hexi more than thirty years, kept his borders and his people, and furthered letters and the faith — the longest-lived of the Five Liang states. Its fall also sounded the end of the Sixteen States age.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 129 (records of Juqu Mengxun), and the *Weishu*, biography of Juqu Mengxun (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 西凉太祖 · 主要事迹

李暠字玄盛，陇西成纪人，自称西汉李广之后。「少而好学，通涉经史」，为北凉段业之敦煌太守。庚子元年，据敦煌自立，称凉公，改元庚子——西凉始。建初元年，迁都酒泉，「以图东向」，欲争河西。

李暠之治，重文教：立泮宫（学校），增高门学生五百人；劝课农桑，教民稼穑；又「以文教致治」，河西文风为之一振。然西凉地狭力弱，介于北凉、柔然之间，境土日蹙。嘉兴元年，李暠崩，谥武昭王；其子李歆继位，与沮渠蒙逊战于蓼泉，兵败身死，西凉亡。

史家评李暠：「英姿杰出，有雄武之略」，然「地不盈百郡，众不过数万」，终非蒙逊之敌。西凉享国二十一年而亡，其政绩虽可观，然处于强邻之间，文治终不敌武功。李氏后裔归北魏、入隋唐，唐高祖李渊自称凉武昭王之后——西凉之亡，而李唐之祖系自此绵延。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷87《凉武昭王传》、卷129《沮渠蒙逊载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Gao, styled Xuansheng, was a man of Chengji in Longxi, claiming descent from the Han general Li Guang. "Studious from youth, learned in the classics and histories," he served as Duan Ye's governor of Dunhuang. In the 1st year of Gengzi he held Dunhuang and styled himself Duke of Liang, opening the era Gengzi — the beginning of Western Liang. In the 1st year of Jianchu he moved the capital to Jiuquan, "looking eastward," to contend for Hexi.

His rule honored letters: he founded an academy, enlarged the students to five hundred, encouraged farming and mulberries, and taught the people husbandry; "governing by culture," he made the letters of Hexi flourish. But Western Liang was cramped and weak, set between Northern Liang and the Rouran, its borders shrinking. He died in the 1st year of Jiaxing, posthumously King Wuzhao; his son Xin succeeded, fought Juqu Mengxun at Liaoquan, fell in battle, and Western Liang perished.

The historians say of him: "of outstanding bearing, with the air of a hero," yet "his land was not a hundred commanderies, his host not ten thousand men" — no match for Mengxun. Western Liang lasted twenty-one years; its government was admirable, but between strong neighbors culture could not hold against arms. His descendants served Northern Wei and passed into the Sui and Tang — the Tang founder Li Yuan claiming descent from King Wuzhao of Liang: the state died, but the Li line ran on to an empire.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 87 (biography of the Martial King of Liang), ch. 129 (records of Juqu Mengxun) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 夏世祖 · 主要事迹

赫连勃勃，匈奴铁弗部人，刘卫辰之子，原名刘勃勃。其父为北魏所灭，勃勃奔后秦，仕姚兴。龙升元年，勃勃叛后秦，自称天王、大单于，国号大夏——「胡夏」始。勃勃以「帝王系天，当以赫连为氏」之义，改姓赫连。

凤翔元年，勃勃发民夫十万筑统万城：以蒸土筑城，锥入一寸，即杀筑者；「筑城之人，无不殒命」。昌武元年，乘刘裕北伐后秦、刘裕南还之机，勃勃取长安，即皇帝位，建都统万。胡夏全盛时，「南据长安，北临大漠」，然其暴政，为十六国之最：史载勃勃「常以所造器械，验其工拙，射甲不入者斩弓人，入则斩甲匠」，日杀工匠数千。

真兴七年，勃勃崩，子赫连昌继位。承光三年，北魏太武帝破统万，昌被擒；其后定胜四年，胡夏为北魏所灭。史家评勃勃：「雄武过人，残忍好杀，虽匈奴之暴，未有甚于此者。」统万城今犹矗立于陕北沙漠中，为其暴政之纪念碑。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷130《赫连勃勃载记》、卷131《赫连昌载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Helian Bobo, originally Liu Bobo, was a Tie Fu Xiongnu, son of Liu Weichen. His father was destroyed by Northern Wei, and Bobo fled to serve Yao Xing of Later Qin. In the 1st year of Longsheng he turned against Later Qin, styled himself Heavenly King and Great Chanyu, and founded the realm Great Xia — "Xia" to history. Taking the surname Helian — "the Son of Heaven, linked to Heaven" — he built his state on war.

In the 1st year of Fengxiang he drove a hundred thousand laborers to build Tongwan: the earth was steamed and pounded, and if an awl could pierce it a finger's depth, the builder was slain — "of the builders, none escaped death." In the 1st year of Changwu, riding Liu Yu's withdrawal south after taking Chang'an, Bobo seized the city and the imperial throne, with Tongwan as his seat. At its height Xia "held Chang'an in the south and faced the great desert in the north"; and its tyranny was the worst of the age: the records say he tested his weapons by their workmanship — if an arrow failed to pierce armor the bowyer died, if it pierced, the armorer — killing thousands of craftsmen a day.

He died in the 7th year of Zhenxing; his son Helian Chang succeeded, and in the 3rd year of Cheng'guang Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei broke Tongwan and took Chang. Xia, fleeing west, was finally destroyed in the 4th year of Dingsheng. The historians say: "of more than common ferocity, cruel and loving slaughter — among the Xiongnu there was none worse." Tongwan's walls still stand in the northern Shaanxi sands — the monument of his tyranny.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 130 (records of Helian Bobo), ch. 131 (records of Helian Chang) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 北燕文成帝 · 主要事迹

冯跋，长乐信都人，汉人。后燕末，慕容熙暴虐，太平元年，冯跋与高云等杀熙，推高云为帝；旋云为离班等所杀，跋即天王位，都龙城——北燕始，为十六国中唯一汉人建立的政权。

冯跋之治，宽和安民：省徭薄赋，劝课农桑，「人皆称便」；又安集流民，赋税宽简；与柔然和亲，稳定北边；兴学校，尊儒学。北燕虽局促辽西，然在十六国后期乱世中，其治实属可观。太平二十二年，冯跋病笃，其弟冯弘杀太子冯翼自立；后弘为北魏所逼，奔高句丽，北燕亡。

史家评冯跋：「宽仁厚德，务存节俭」，然「保境安民，不能进取中原」。北燕以汉人政权立于胡族环伺之中，享国二十余年，赖其宽政与和亲；然终因国力微弱，为北魏所并。北燕之亡，五胡十六国之局亦近尾声。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷125《冯跋载记》、卷125《冯弘载记》及《魏书·冯跋传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

史家评冯跋：「宽仁厚德，务存节俭」，然「保境安民，不能进取中原」。北燕以汉人政权立于胡族环伺之中，享国二十余年，赖其宽政与和亲；然终因国力微弱，为北魏所并。北燕之亡，五胡十六国之局亦近尾声。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷125《冯跋载记》、卷125《冯弘载记》及《魏书·冯跋传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Feng Ba was a Han of Xindu in Changle. In the last years of Later Yan the emperor Murong Xi was a tyrant; in the 1st year of Taiping Ba and Gao Yun and the others slew Xi and set up Yun; when Yun was slain by Li Ban and the rest, Ba took the heavenly throne himself, with his capital at Longcheng — the beginning of Northern Yan, the one Han-founded state of the Sixteen.

His rule was lenient and pacific: he lightened corvée and taxes, encouraged farming and mulberries, "and the people praised it"; he gathered the refugees and made the levies easy; he married peace with the Rouran, steadying the northern border; he founded schools and honored Confucian learning. Cramped in Liaoxi though it was, Northern Yan's government was among the most admirable of the later Sixteen States. In the 22nd year of Taiping, as Ba lay ill, his brother Feng Hong slew the heir Feng Yi and took the throne; pressed by Northern Wei, Hong fled to Goguryeo, and Northern Yan was no more.

The historians say of Ba: "benevolent and generous, careful in economy," yet "he held his borders and cared for his people, but could not press into the Central Plains." A Han regime ringed by barbarian states, Northern Yan held on over twenty years by its lenient rule and its marriages of peace; and with its fall, the Sixteen States age itself drew to its end.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 125 (records of Feng Ba), ch. 125 (records of Feng Hong), and the *Weishu*, biography of Feng Ba (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 前凉武王 · 主要事迹

张轨字士彦，安定乌氏人，「明敏好学，有器望」。永宁元年，八王之乱方炽，轨请为凉州刺史，遂据河西。时中原大乱，轨保境安民，劝课农桑，立学校，「凉州自轨以来，号为乐土」——西晋士民避乱者，多归凉州。

张轨之治：讨破鲜卑若罗拔能，威行河西；以周玘等为谋主，兴文教、置学官；「忠于晋室」，贡献不绝，受西晋封爵。建兴二年，张轨病卒，谥武公，子寔继位。张氏世守凉州，历九主七十六年（301-376），为十六国中命祚最长者——前凉虽未称帝，然其据河西自守，实为一方之政权。

史家评张轨：「怀抚羌胡，化行河右。」在中原板荡之际，凉州独保太平，衣冠南渡之外，更有士人西走凉州——「凉州之畜为天下饶」，张轨之治，为乱世中之净土。其子孙后为前秦所灭，然前凉之德，犹为后世所称。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷86《张轨传》、卷86《张寔传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Zhang Gui, styled Shiyan, was a man of Wushi in Anding, "sharp and studious, of high repute." In the 1st year of Yongning, with the War of the Eight Princes blazing, he asked for the governorship of Liangzhou and held Hexi. While the Central Plains collapsed he kept his borders and his people, encouraged farming and mulberries, and founded schools — "Liangzhou, since Gui, was called the land of delight" — and the gentry and refugees of the Jin fled west to him.

His rule: he broke the Xianbei Ruoluo Baneng and his name ran through Hexi; with Zhou Qi and the others as counselors he furthered letters and established academies; "loyal to the Jin house," he never ceased tribute and received Jin's titles. He died of illness in the 2nd year of Jianxing, posthumously Duke Wu, and his son Shi succeeded. The Zhang house held Liangzhou through nine rulers and seventy-six years (301–376), the longest-lived of the Sixteen States — though it never took the imperial title, its self-ruling Hexi was a true power.

The historians say of him: "he cherished the Qiang and the Hu, and carried civilization through the river lands." While the Central Plains went under, Liangzhou alone kept its peace; besides the caps and gowns crossing south, there was a westward flight of scholars — "Liangzhou's cattle were the realm's wealth" — and Gui's rule was a refuge in the storm. His descendants were later swept away by Former Qin, but the virtue of Former Liang was long remembered.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 86 (biography of Zhang Gui), ch. 86 (biography of Zhang Shi) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

In the 39th year of Jianguo Former Qin destroyed it; Northern Wei later honored him as Emperor Zhaocheng.

emperors.bio_md:
# 代王 · 主要事迹

拓跋什翼犍，拓跋鲜卑首领，拓跋郁律之子。幼年质于后赵，见识中原制度。建国元年，什翼犍即代王位，建元建国，都云中盛乐——代国自此有年号、有都城，渐脱部落之习。

什翼犍之治，为拓跋部由部落联盟向国家过渡之关键：始制法律，「法令明整」；分土定居，「分筑城郭」；又置百官，仿晋制。军事上，屡北征高车、西击刘卫辰，代北强盛。建国三十九年，前秦苻坚遣军大举来攻，代国诸部溃散，什翼犍为其庶子寔君所杀（一说为苻坚所害），代国亡。

代国虽亡，然拓跋之根未绝：什翼犍之孙拓跋珪，于淝水之战后复国，改称魏，是为北魏道武帝。北魏追尊什翼犍为昭成皇帝。史家论什翼犍：立法建国，开北魏之先河——五胡诸国多旋兴旋亡，而拓跋氏历亡而不绝，终统一北方，其奠基之功，实自什翼犍始。

> 本地参考：点校本《魏书》卷1《序纪》、卷113《官氏志》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Tuoba Shiyijian was a chief of the Tuoba Xianbei, son of Tuoba Yulü. In his youth he was a hostage in Later Zhao and saw the institutions of the Central Plains. In the 1st year of Jianguo he took the throne as King of Dai, opened the era Jianguo, and made Shengle in Yunzhong his capital — the Dai realm now had its own era and capital, and began to leave the tribal way behind.

His reign marks the passage of the Tuoba from tribal league to state: he first fixed the laws, "clear and strict"; he allotted the lands for settlement and "built walled towns"; he installed his officials on the Jin model. In arms he campaigned north again and again against the Gaoche and west against Liu Weichen, and the north grew strong under him. In the 39th year of Jianguo, Fu Jian of Former Qin came against him in force; the tribes scattered, and Shiyijian was slain by his own son Shijun (or, some say, by Fu Jian's men) — the Dai realm was no more.

But the Tuoba root was not cut: his grandson Tuoba Gui, after the Fei River defeat, restored the state under the name Wei — Emperor Daowu of Northern Wei. Northern Wei honored Shiyijian as Emperor Zhaocheng. The historians see in him the maker of the laws and statehood of the Tuoba, the forerunner of Northern Wei: of all the barbarian states, only the Tuoba fell and rose again to unite the north — and the foundation was laid by Shiyijian.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Weishu*, ch. 1 ("Prefatory Annals"), ch. 113 (treatise on official clans) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 西夏景宗 · 主要事迹

李元昊是西夏实际的开国之主。1032 年父李德明卒，他袭夏王位，随即加速去宋化与民族国家建构；1038 年在兴庆府即皇帝位，国号大夏，改元天授礼法延祚，正式与宋、辽并立。本页以《宋史·卷485·夏国传》为年表主线，《辽史》相关纪为二手入口。

称帝前后，他完成了一整套国族符号与制度建构：命野利仁荣等造番书（西夏文），改服饰官制，又设中书、枢密等机构，番汉分号。这套"强化主体性"的路线，与[[n-wei-xiaowen|北魏孝文帝]]的汉化改革恰好方向相反，对读可见中古北方政权处理自身身份的两种极端路径。

武功方面，约 1036 年他攻取瓜、沙、肃等河西走廊要地，奠定称帝版图——这条走廊正是[[han-wu-di|汉武帝]]时代开通的西北命脉，千年之后成为大夏立国的根基。1040 年三川口、1041 年好水川、1042 年定川寨，夏军连续三年重创宋军，确立了西夏的军事地位；好水川一役尤为宋夏战争的名场面（互见《宋史》任福等列传）。

连战之后是外交收尾。1044 年宋夏达成庆历和议：元昊对宋称臣而自帝其国，以名实分离换取岁赐与边境稳定；同年与辽冲突后言和，在宋、辽、夏三角之间周旋得体。文治、武功、韬略三线，至此把一个河西政权立成了鼎立之一极。

1048 年，元昊在宫廷斗争中被刺死，幼主谅祚继立，外戚没藏氏掌权——国祚并未随他个人终结，西夏转入后续诸帝。需要说明的是，宋、辽史书对西夏站位偏贬，本项目月旦取中；西夏文创制等细节仍待专书补证。

的汉化改革恰好方向相反，对读可见中古北方政权处理自身身份的两种极端路径。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Yuanhao was the de facto founder of Western Xia. In 1032 his father Li Deming died and he succeeded as Prince of Xia, at once accelerating de-Songification and nation-building; in 1038 he proclaimed himself emperor at Xingqing, took the dynastic name Great Xia, and changed the era to Tianshou Lifa Yanzuo, formally standing alongside Song and Liao. This page takes 《宋史·卷485·夏国传》 as the backbone of its chronology, with the relevant annals of 《辽史》 as a secondary entry point.

Around his proclamation he completed a whole set of national symbols and institutions: he ordered Yeli Renrong and others to devise the Tangut script, reformed dress and officialdom, and established organs such as the Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs under separate Tangut and Han designations. This line of "asserting distinctiveness" ran in exactly the opposite direction from the sinicization of

; read together, they show the two extreme paths by which medieval northern regimes handled their own identity.

On the military side, around 1036 he seized Gua, Sha, Su, and other key points of the Hexi Corridor, laying the territorial foundation for his imperial claim—the very corridor opened in the age of

as the northwest lifeline, which a thousand years later became the ground on which Great Xia was founded. At Sanchuankou in 1040, Haoshuichuan in 1041, and Dingchuanzhai in 1042, Xia forces mauled the Song armies three years running and established Western Xia's military standing; Haoshuichuan in particular is the famous set piece of the Song–Xia war (cross-referenced in the biographies of Ren Fu and others in 《宋史》).

After the string of victories came the diplomatic wrap-up. In 1044 Song and Xia reached the Qingli settlement: Yuanhao styled himself a subject toward Song while reigning as emperor within his own realm, trading the split between name and fact for annual payments and a stable border; the same year, after clashes with Liao, he made peace, maneuvering deftly within the Song–Liao–Xia triangle. Civil construction, military success, and statecraft together had by now raised a Hexi regime into one pole of a tripartite standoff.

In 1048 Yuanhao was stabbed to death amid palace struggles; the child ruler Liangzuo succeeded, and the consort clan Mozang took power—the dynasty did not end with his person, and Western Xia passed to its later rulers. It should be noted that Song and Liao historiography is biased against Western Xia, so this project's appraisal takes a middle position; details such as the creation of the Tangut script still await confirmation from specialized scholarship.

emperors.bio_md:
# 南唐后主 · 主要事迹

李煜是南唐末主。宋建隆二年（961），中主李璟卒，李煜继位于金陵，此时南唐对宋已处劣势。本页以《宋史·卷478·南唐世家》为年表主线，《宋史·太祖纪》编年互见（本地参考库已备）。

开宝前后（971），他去帝号、称江南国主，对宋称臣以求苟安；在位间倾力于书画音律词章，文艺成就远超君道事功。

开宝七年（974），曹彬等率宋师南下伐江南，兵临长江；开宝八年（975）宋军破金陵，后主出降，南唐亡。此役出自[[n-song-tai-zu|宋太祖]]朝平江南的部署，可与宋方本纪对读。

开宝九年（976）他北迁汴京，封违命侯，软禁中词多故国之思。太平兴国三年（978）卒于京师，时宋太宗在位；民间有七夕赐牵机药传说，正史记载简略，此处作待考处理。

他的后效在文学：二主词为词史入口，君道失败与词人成就分离，后世月旦常带同情分。与南唐元宗（中主李璟）对读，可见南唐自中主至后主两代而终的格局。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Yu was the last ruler of the Southern Tang. In the second year of the Song Jianlong era (961), the Middle Ruler Li Jing died, and Li Yu succeeded to the throne at Jinling, with Southern Tang already at a disadvantage against the Song. This page takes 《宋史·卷478·南唐世家》 as the chronological backbone, cross-checked against the annals in 《宋史·太祖纪》 (available in the local reference library).

Around the Kaibao era (971), he renounced the imperial title, styled himself Ruler of Jiangnan, and submitted to the Song as a vassal in search of a precarious peace; throughout his reign he poured his energy into painting, calligraphy, music, and verse, and his literary achievement far outran his record as a sovereign.

In the seventh year of Kaibao (974), Cao Bin and others led the Song army south against Jiangnan and brought it to the banks of the Yangtze; in the eighth year (975) Song forces breached Jinling, the Last Ruler came out and surrendered, and Southern Tang fell. This campaign grew out of the Jiangnan strategy of

's court and can be read against the Song-side basic annals.

In the ninth year of Kaibao (976) he was moved north to Bianjing and enfeoffed as the Marquis of Weiming; in confinement his ci poems dwelled on longing for his lost realm. He died at the capital in the third year of Taiping Xingguo (978), while Emperor Taizong of Song was on the throne; a folk legend holds that poison was granted to him on the Double Seventh night, but the standard histories record little, and the matter is treated here as unverified.

His afterlife lies in literature: the ci of the Two Rulers are an entryway into the history of the genre, his failure as a sovereign is read apart from his achievement as a poet, and later judgment has often carried a measure of sympathy. Read alongside Southern Tang Yuanzong (the Middle Ruler Li Jing), the page shows the shape of a Southern Tang that ran its course in two generations, from the Middle Ruler to the Last Ruler.

emperors.summary: 受禅代周、灭陈混一南北，以开皇制度奠定后世政制底盘，却因晚年废立与二世而亡留下争议的开国之主。
emperors.summary_en: Founding ruler who received Northern Zhou's abdication to establish the Sui and destroyed Chen to reunify north and south, laying the institutional foundation for later dynasties through the Kaihuang system, yet left controversy through the late-life change of heir and the dynasty's fall in the second generation.

timeline.title: 代周建隋
timeline.summary: 受北周禅让建隋，改元开皇，北周亡。
timeline.summary_en: He received Northern Zhou's abdication and founded the Sui, changing the era name to Kaihuang; Northern Zhou ended.

timeline.title: 尽灭北周宗室隐患
timeline.title_en: Purging the Northern Zhou Royal House
timeline.summary: 开国之初以政治清洗巩固新朝（克制叙述）。
timeline.summary_en: In the founding's early days he consolidated the new dynasty through political purges (restrained account).

timeline.title: 迁大兴城
timeline.summary: 营迁大兴（新长安），都城格局一新。
timeline.summary_en: He built and moved the capital to Daxing (the new Chang'an), giving the capital an entirely new layout.

timeline.title: 灭后梁
timeline.summary: 江陵后梁亡，为南进混一的前奏。
timeline.summary_en: The Later Liang at Jiangling fell, a prelude to the southern advance and reunification.

timeline.title: 灭陈混一
timeline.summary: 平陈，南北再统一，史称混一戎夏。
timeline.summary_en: Chen was pacified and north and south reunified, known in history as "the unification of the realm".

timeline.title: 江南反隋平定
timeline.summary: 灭陈后江南叛乱被平定，统一局面巩固。
timeline.summary_en: After Chen's fall, the Jiangnan rebellions were suppressed and the unified order was consolidated.

timeline.title: 废太子勇
timeline.summary: 废黜太子杨勇，储位动摇。
timeline.summary_en: Crown Prince Yang Yong was deposed, and the succession was shaken.

timeline.title: 废勇立广
timeline.summary: 立晋王广为太子，种下国祚风险。
timeline.summary_en: The Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, was made crown prince, planting a risk to the dynasty's fortunes.

timeline.title: 改元仁寿
timeline.summary: 晚年改元，储位已定。
timeline.summary_en: The era name was changed in his final years, with the heir already settled.

timeline.title: 仁寿宫事
timeline.summary: 卧病仁寿宫，遗命与继位过程史有异说（克制叙述）。
timeline.summary_en: He lay ill at Renshou Palace; the record diverges on his dying orders and the succession process (restrained account).

timeline.title: 文帝崩
timeline.summary: 崩于仁寿宫，炀帝即位；统一遗产与二世风险同时交接。
timeline.summary_en: He died at Renshou Palace and Emperor Yang ascended; the legacy of unification and the risk of a second-generation collapse were handed over together.

timeline.title: 开皇制度
timeline.summary: 三省六部成型、统一货币度量、检括户口，奠定后世政制底盘。
timeline.summary_en: The Three Departments and Six Ministries took shape, currency and weights and measures were unified, and households were registered and checked, laying the institutional foundation for later dynasties.

开皇九年灭陈（陈后主），南北混一（页待建）
长期分裂后混一、却二世而危的长线对照

meta.inclusion_reason: 结束近三百年分裂、混一南北的开国之主，正史立纪。

emperors.bio_md:
# 隋文帝 · 主要事迹

杨坚以受禅方式代北周建隋，改元开皇。新朝初立，一面以政治手段清除北周宗室隐患、稳住局面，一面营迁大兴城，重定都城格局——开国的前几步，走得谨慎而彻底。

开皇七年，江陵后梁亡，南进之门洞开；开皇九年平陈，自东晋以来近三百年的南北分裂宣告结束，史称「混一戎夏」。次年江南反隋势力被平定，统一局面真正巩固。灭陈一役虽由诸将执行，战略决断皆出朝廷。

混一之外，开皇间三省六部成型、统一货币度量、检括户口，奠定此后数百年的政制底盘，后效极高。论文治的制度遗产，隋文帝在历代开国之主中位置很靠前。

晚年却是另一番走向：开皇二十年废太子勇、改立晋王广，储位之争自此埋下国祚风险。仁寿四年，文帝崩于仁寿宫，遗命与继位过程史有异说。其子[[sui-yang|隋炀帝]]即位，统一遗产与二世风险同时交接——废立争议与「二世而亡」的结局，压低了后世对这场开国之局的评价。与[[qin-shi-huang|秦始皇]]对读：二者皆在长期分裂后完成混一，又皆在二代迅速陷入危局，是读统一帝国史绕不开的一对对照。

对读：二者皆在长期分裂后完成混一，又皆在二代迅速陷入危局，是读统一帝国史绕不开的一对对照。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yang Jian replaced Northern Zhou and founded the Sui through an abdication, changing the era name to Kaihuang. With the new dynasty just established, he used political means to remove the lingering threat of the Northern Zhou royal house and steady the situation, while building and moving to Daxing and redesigning the capital's layout — the founding's first steps were taken with caution and thoroughness.

In Kaihuang 7, the Later Liang at Jiangling fell and the gate to the southern advance swung open; in Kaihuang 9 Chen was pacified, ending the nearly three-hundred-year division of north and south since the Eastern Jin — known in history as "the unification of the realm". The following year the anti-Sui forces in Jiangnan were suppressed, and the unified order was truly consolidated. Though the destruction of Chen was executed by his generals, every strategic decision came from the court.

Beyond unification, the Kaihuang era saw the Three Departments and Six Ministries take shape, currency and weights and measures unified, and households registered and checked — laying the institutional foundation of government for centuries to come, with exceptionally far-reaching aftereffects. In terms of institutional legacy, Emperor Wen ranks near the very front among the founding rulers of successive dynasties.

His later years took a different course: in Kaihuang 20 he deposed Crown Prince Yang Yong and installed the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, in his place — and the struggle over the succession thereafter planted a risk to the dynasty's fortunes. In Renshou 4, Emperor Wen died at Renshou Palace; the historical record diverges on his dying orders and the succession process. His son

took the throne, and the legacy of unification was handed over together with the risk of a second-generation collapse — the controversy over the change of heir and the ending of "falling in the second generation" lowered later generations' appraisal of this founding. Read alongside
: both completed reunification after long division, and both quickly plunged into crisis in the second generation — an unavoidable pair for anyone reading the history of unified empires.

emperors.bio_md:
# 隋炀帝 · 主要事迹

杨广本为晋王，开皇九年（589）参与平陈立功，开皇二十年（600）被立为太子，仁寿四年（604）即帝位，后改元大业。本页以《隋书·炀帝纪》为年表主线，辅以《资治通鉴·隋纪》编年对照。

大业年间他接连启动超大规模的工程与行动：大业元年（605）营建东都洛阳，开通济渠等运河段，贯通南北水运；大业四年（608）又开永济渠北通涿郡；大业五年（609）西巡张掖，西域胡商前来朝会，一时呈现盛世表象。东都与运河构成他最重要的后效遗产，但征发之巨也同步消耗着帝国的根本。

转折出现在大业八年（612）一征高句丽：大举东征，丧师费财，国内矛盾激化。次年（613）再征辽东，杨玄感起兵，崩坏加速。大业十二年（616）他三幸江都，中原随之失控；大业十三年（617）群雄并起，中枢名存实亡；大业十四年（618），宇文化及等发动江都之变，炀帝身死，隋亡。

后世对他月旦极低，而运河、东都与沟通南北的后效深远。与[[sui-wen|隋文帝]]对读，可见开皇一朝的积累如何在大业年间被推向极致并耗尽；与[[tang-tai-zong|唐太宗]]对读，可见唐承隋制的承接与反拨。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yang Guang was originally the Prince of Jin. In Kaihuang 9 (589) he took part in the pacification of Chen and earned merit; in Kaihuang 20 (600) he was made crown prince; in Renshou 4 (604) he ascended the throne, later changing the era name to Daye. This page follows the Annals of Emperor Yang in the Book of Sui as its chronological spine, cross-checked against the Sui chapters of the Zizhi Tongjian.

During the Daye era he launched one outsized project and operation after another: in Daye 1 (605) he built the Eastern Capital at Luoyang and dug the Tongji Canal and other canal sections, linking north-south water transport; in Daye 4 (608) he dug the Yongji Canal, reaching Zhuo Commandery in the north; in Daye 5 (609) he toured west to Zhangye, where Hu merchants from the Western Regions came to court, presenting for a time the appearance of a flourishing age. The Eastern Capital and the canals form his most important lasting legacy, yet the sheer scale of conscription was simultaneously consuming the empire's foundations.

The turning point came in Daye 8 (612) with the first campaign against Goguryeo: a massive eastern expedition that lost armies and drained wealth, intensifying domestic tensions. The following year (613) he campaigned in Liaodong again, and Yang Xuangan rose in revolt, accelerating the collapse. In Daye 12 (616) he went to Jiangdu for the third time, and the Central Plains slipped from control; in Daye 13 (617) warlords rose on all sides and the central authority existed in name only; in Daye 14 (618), Yuwen Huaji and others launched the Jiangdu coup, Emperor Yang was killed, and the Sui fell.

Later generations judged him extremely harshly, yet the lasting effects of the canals, the Eastern Capital, and the linking of north and south run deep. Read alongside
, one can see how the accumulation of the Kaihuang era was pushed to the extreme and exhausted during the Daye years; read alongside
, one can see how the Tang both inherited and reacted against Sui institutions.

# 唐太宗 · 主要事迹

李世民以秦王定天下、以玄武门入承大统，贞观一朝以用人与纳谏闻名，并在北境与辽东方向留下清晰的军事地理轨迹。本页主据两唐书太宗本纪与《资治通鉴·唐纪》（本地参考库已备；旧/新唐书 PDF 请自行核验完整性）。

本图鉴同时收录其即位前关键节点（晋阳起兵），以便地图连成一条「从河东到长安、再向北与东」的人生线。与[[han-wu-di|汉武帝]]对读，可看不同时代的「极盛叙事」；与[[qin-shi-huang|秦始皇]]对读，可看统一帝国传统下治理风格的差异。

emperors.bio_md:
# 武则天 · 主要事迹

武则天是中国史上唯一正式称帝的女皇帝。本页以《旧唐书·则天皇后本纪》为年表主线，辅以《新唐书》与《资治通鉴·唐纪》编年（本地参考库已备）。她贞观十一年入宫为[[tang-tai-zong|唐太宗]]才人，历感业寺环节后重返宫廷，永徽六年由昭仪立为皇后——废王立武之争中，长孙无忌等元老反对派相继贬死，她由此进入权力中枢。

显庆五年后高宗多病，天后参决政务，朝中形成"二圣"格局。弘道元年高宗崩于洛阳，中宗即位，她临朝称制；次年即废中宗为庐陵王，改立睿宗而实掌朝政。垂拱四年洛阳明堂建成，铜匦告密与酷吏政治并行，恩威双轨的统治术于此成型。

天授元年，她在神都洛阳加尊号、改国号为周，正式称帝，女主称制由事实变为名分。在位期间破格用人、发展科举殿试，神功元年狄仁杰入相成为能吏政治的代表节点；文治实绩与酷吏之治始终并存，构成武周的一体两面。

神龙元年，张柬之等发动政变拥中宗复位，武周终结，则天迁宫。旧史多以"女祸"叙事贬抑，今人则更重估其制度与人事遗产——本图鉴月旦中性偏下，留给读者对读：从入宫才人到革唐为周，再到还政李唐，与[[tang-xian-zong|唐宪宗]]的中兴对照，可见唐室中衰与重建的完整弧线。

bio_parts_en.value: Wu Zetian is the only woman in Chinese history to have formally taken the imperial title. This page builds its chronology on the "Basic Annals of Empress Zetian" in the Old Book of Tang, supplemented by the New Book of Tang and the Tang chronicle of the Zizhi Tongjian (all held in the local reference library). She entered the palace in Zhenguan 11 as a cairen consort of

and, after the Ganye Temple episode, returned to the court; in Yonghui 6 she was raised from zhaoyi to empress. In the struggle over deposing Empress Wang for Wu, veteran opponents such as Zhangsun Wuji were demoted and died one after another, and through this she entered the center of power.

After Xianqing 5, as Gaozong fell frequently ill, the Heavenly Empress joined in deciding state affairs and a "Two Sages" arrangement took shape at court. In Hongdao 1 Gaozong died in Luoyang; Zhongzong succeeded and she ruled from behind the screen. The very next year she deposed Zhongzong to Prince of Luling, installed Ruizong instead, and held real power over the court. In Chuigong 4 the Bright Hall in Luoyang was completed, while copper-box informant reports and the politics of harsh officials ran in tandem: her dual-track statecraft of favor and fear took form here.

In Tianshou 1, at the Divine Capital Luoyang, she took a new honorific title, changed the dynastic name to Zhou, and formally assumed the throne; rule by a female sovereign passed from fact into name. During her reign she broke conventions in appointing talent and developed the palace examination within the imperial examinations, and in Shengong 1 Di Renjie's entry as chancellor became the representative node of capable-official politics. Solid civil achievements and the rule of harsh officials coexisted throughout, forming the two faces of Wu Zhou.

In Shenlong 1, Zhang Jianzhi and others launched a coup that restored Zhongzong; Wu Zhou ended and Zetian moved to another palace. The old histories mostly belittled her through the "female calamity" narrative, while today her institutional and personnel legacy is being revalued. This atlas's appraisal is neutral to mildly negative, left for readers to weigh against the evidence: from palace cairen to changing Tang into Zhou and then returning power to the Li Tang house, read alongside the restoration of
, one can see the full arc of the Tang house's mid-course decline and rebuilding.

emperors.summary_en: A mid-Tang emperor whose fifteen-year reign centered on reducing the military provinces, pacifying Xichuan, breaking Huaixi, and overawing Heshuo to achieve the Yuanhe Restoration, before dying suddenly amid suspicions involving eunuchs.

timeline.title: 即位
timeline.summary: 顺宗内禅，即帝位；朝廷人事与年号随之更始，明年改元元和。
timeline.summary_en: Shunzong abdicates within the family and he takes the throne; court personnel and the era name are renewed, and the next year changes to Yuanhe.

timeline.title: 平夏绥杨惠琳
timeline.summary: 讨平夏绥杨惠琳，削藩早期胜利。
timeline.summary_en: Suppresses Yang Huilin of Xia-Sui, an early victory in reducing the provinces.

timeline.title: 平西川
timeline.summary: 讨平西川刘辟，展示削藩决心。
timeline.summary_en: Suppresses Liu Pi of Xichuan, demonstrating the resolve to reduce the provinces.

timeline.title: 成德王承宗战事
timeline.summary: 讨成德王承宗，成果有限，显示削藩难度。
timeline.summary_en: Campaigns against Wang Chengzong of Chengde with limited results, showing how hard province reduction is.

timeline.title: 李师道刺武元衡
timeline.summary: 藩镇以恐怖手段刺杀宰相武元衡于长安，朝野震动。
timeline.summary_en: A military province has the chancellor Wu Yuanheng assassinated in Chang'an by terror tactics, shocking court and country.

timeline.title: 裴度宣慰淮西
timeline.summary: 宰相裴度赴淮西督师宣慰，为雪夜入蔡的政治背景。
timeline.summary_en: Chancellor Pei Du goes to Huaixi to direct and reassure the armies, the political backdrop to the snowy-night entry into Cai.

timeline.title: 平淮西
timeline.summary: 李愬雪夜入蔡州，擒吴元济，元和削藩达到高潮。
timeline.summary_en: Li Su enters Caizhou on a snowy night and captures Wu Yuanji, the high point of Yuanhe province reduction.

timeline.title: 成德归朝
timeline.summary: 成德等河朔藩镇一度听命朝廷，元和中兴气象达到高点。
timeline.summary_en: Chengde and other Heshuo provinces for a time obey the court, and the Yuanhe Restoration reaches its peak.

timeline.title: 迎佛骨
timeline.summary: 迎法门寺佛骨入长安；韩愈上表极谏，贬逐出京。
timeline.summary_en: The Famen Temple Buddha relic is received into Chang'an; Han Yu submits a memorial of utmost remonstrance and is banished from the capital.

timeline.title: 穆宗即位
timeline.summary: 宪宗崩后穆宗立，朝廷人事与年号更始，削藩回落。
timeline.summary_en: After Xianzong's death Muzong succeeds; court personnel and the era name are renewed, and province reduction recedes.

timeline.title: 暴崩
timeline.summary: 暴崩于长安，史载与宦官相关的疑云，削藩成果随之回落。
timeline.summary_en: Dies suddenly in Chang'an; the histories record suspicions involving eunuchs, and the gains of province reduction recede.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐宪宗 · 主要事迹

李纯在位十五年（805—820），年号元和，是安史之乱后唐朝最有振作气象的皇帝。本页以《旧唐书·宪宗纪》为年表主线，辅以《新唐书·宪宗纪》与《资治通鉴》编年对照（本地参考库已备）。他的一生主线只有两个字：削藩。

元和元年（806）是他开局的手笔：先是讨平夏绥杨惠琳，继而讨平西川刘辟——两战皆捷，向天下藩镇展示了朝廷不再姑息的决心。但元和四年（809）讨伐成德王承宗一役成果有限，也让他看清河朔藩镇根深蒂固、硬啃不易的现实。

真正的考验在淮西。元和十年（815），平卢李师道竟遣刺客在长安街头杀死主战宰相武元衡，朝野震动，而朝廷用兵之志未移。元和十二年（817），宰相裴度亲赴淮西宣慰督师，名将李愬雪夜奇袭入蔡州，生擒吴元济——这是元和削藩的高潮，也是中唐最著名的一场奇袭。次年（818）前后，成德等河朔强藩一度听命于朝，史称"元和中兴"。

晚年他迎法门寺佛骨入长安，韩愈上表极谏而被贬，留下君臣关系与信仰政策的另一面相。元和十五年（820），他在长安暴崩，史载此事笼罩着与宦官相关的疑云；唐穆宗即位后，削藩成果迅速回落，河朔此后复叛。从唐顺宗的永贞内禅开局，到暴崩落幕，"元和中兴"是否可持续，正是读宪宗一朝最值得停下来的问题；与[[tang-tai-zong|唐太宗]]的贞观范式对读，也可见盛唐与中唐之间帝国处境的巨大落差。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Chun reigned for fifteen years (805–820) under the era name Yuanhe and was the most revitalizing emperor of the Tang after the An Lushan Rebellion. This page builds its chronology on the "Annals of Xianzong" in the Old Book of Tang, checked against the "Annals of Xianzong" in the New Book of Tang and the Zizhi Tongjian (all held in the local reference library). The main line of his life comes down to two words: reducing the provinces.

Yuanhe 1 (806) showed his opening hand: first he suppressed Yang Huilin of Xia-Sui, then Liu Pi of Xichuan. Two victories in a row announced to every military province that the court would no longer be lenient. But the campaign against Wang Chengzong of Chengde in Yuanhe 4 (809) achieved limited results, and it taught him how deeply entrenched the Heshuo provinces were and how hard they would be to crack.

The real test was Huaixi. In Yuanhe 10 (815), Li Shidao of Pinglu sent assassins who killed the pro-war chancellor Wu Yuanheng in the streets of Chang'an, shocking court and country, yet the court's will to use force did not waver. In Yuanhe 12 (817) the chancellor Pei Du went in person to Huaixi to reassure and direct the armies, and the renowned general Li Su made a surprise entry into Caizhou on a snowy night and captured Wu Yuanji alive: the climax of Yuanhe province reduction and the most celebrated surprise attack of the mid-Tang. Around the following year (818), powerful Heshuo provinces such as Chengde for a time obeyed the court, in what the histories call the "Yuanhe Restoration."

In his later years he received the Buddha's relic from Famen Temple into Chang'an; Han Yu submitted a memorial of utmost remonstrance and was banished, leaving another face of ruler-minister relations and religious policy. In Yuanhe 15 (820) he died suddenly in Chang'an, an event the histories record as wrapped in suspicions involving eunuchs. After Emperor Muzong of Tang took the throne, the gains of province reduction quickly receded and Heshuo rebelled again. From the Yongzhen abdication of Shunzong at the opening to the sudden death at the close, whether the "Yuanhe Restoration" could have lasted is the question most worth pausing over in Xianzong's reign; read against the Zhenguan model of
, it also shows the enormous gap in the empire's circumstances between the High Tang and the mid-Tang.

emperors.summary: 在位六年，高平破敌、三征淮南、北伐收复三关，以整军与改革为北宋统一奠基的英年早逝之主。
emperors.summary_en: An emperor who died young after only six years on the throne, breaking the enemy at Gaoping, campaigning thrice in Huainan, and recovering the Three Passes in a northern expedition, whose military reorganization and reforms laid the foundation for Northern Song unification.

portrait.appearance_basis: 传统画像符号化描写居多。MVP 用占位图；定稿前依时代冠服作艺术想象。

timeline.title: 即位
timeline.summary: 郭威崩，柴荣即位，是为世宗。
timeline.summary_en: Guo Wei dies and Chai Rong takes the throne, becoming Shizong.

timeline.title: 沿用显德年号
timeline.summary: 郭威正月改广顺四年为显德元年；荣即位后沿用，朝廷人事更始。
timeline.summary_en: Guo Wei changes Guangshun 4 into Xiande 1 in the first month; Chai Rong keeps it after his accession as court personnel are renewed.

timeline.title: 高平之战
timeline.summary: 亲征败北汉、契丹联军于高平，战后整肃禁军，确立权威。
timeline.summary_en: Campaigns in person and defeats the allied Northern Han and Khitan army at Gaoping, then purges the palace army and establishes his authority.

timeline.title: 毁佛铸钱
timeline.summary: 限寺减僧，毁铜佛铸钱，以充财政军备。
timeline.summary_en: Restricts temples and reduces the clergy, melting bronze Buddha statues for coin to fund finances and armament.

timeline.title: 整军均田
timeline.summary: 选练禁军、限制寺院、均定田赋，国力回升。
timeline.summary_en: Selects and trains the palace army, restricts temples, and equalizes land taxes; state power recovers.

timeline.title: 征淮南
timeline.summary: 亲征南唐，显德振旅。
timeline.summary_en: Campaigns in person against Southern Tang; the Xiande armies are invigorated.

timeline.title: 经略淮南
timeline.summary: 多次征南唐，南压强敌，指向江北诸州。
timeline.summary_en: Campaigns repeatedly against Southern Tang, pressing the strong enemy in the south toward the prefectures north of the river.

timeline.title: 江北十四州
timeline.summary: 南唐献江北之地，周取十四州。
timeline.summary_en: Southern Tang cedes the lands north of the river and Zhou takes fourteen prefectures.

timeline.title: 北伐契丹
timeline.summary: 亲率北伐，收复关南部分州县，病重回师。
timeline.summary_en: Leads the northern expedition in person, recovers some Guannan prefectures, and returns gravely ill.

timeline.title: 收复三关
timeline.summary: 北伐取关南三州，混一之志未竟而病重。
timeline.summary_en: The northern expedition takes three prefectures in Guannan; his ambition to unify goes unfulfilled as his illness worsens.

timeline.title: 遗命范质等
timeline.summary: 病重托孤于范质等，身后旋有陈桥之变。
timeline.summary_en: Gravely ill, he entrusts his heir to Fan Zhi and others; the Chenqiao Mutiny follows soon after his death.

timeline.title: 世宗崩
timeline.summary: 崩于开封，子宗训年幼继位，旋有陈桥兵变，周禅于宋。
timeline.summary_en: Dies at Kaifeng; his young son Zongxun succeeds, the Chenqiao Mutiny soon follows, and Zhou yields to Song.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后周世宗 · 主要事迹

柴荣在位不过六年，却是五代末局里承前启后的枢纽：上接养父后周太祖郭威的草创之业，下开[[n-song-tai-zu|宋太祖]]赵匡胤的统一之局。本页以《旧五代史·周书·世宗纪》为年表主线，辅以《新五代史·周本纪》与《资治通鉴》编年（本地参考库已备）。

显德元年，郭威崩，柴荣即位，沿用显德年号。北汉与契丹联军压境，他亲征迎战，败之于高平，战后整肃禁军，一战确立新君权威。内政上同样果决：显德二年限寺减僧、毁铜佛铸钱以充财政军备；显德间又选练禁军、均定田赋，使国力回升。

南方，他连年亲征南唐，显德三年起兵，四至五年间反复经略淮南，至显德五年南唐献出江北之地，周取十四州，把疆界推到长江北岸——这正是后来[[n-tang-houzhu|南唐后主]]一系被动局面的先声。显德六年，他转而北伐契丹，收复关南三关州县，兵锋直指幽州方向，却于军中病重，只得回师。

回到开封后，他托孤于范质等，旋即驾崩，子宗训年幼继位。次年陈桥兵变，周禅于宋，他未竟的混一之志由宋人接手完成。史家每论其英年早逝：若得永年，宋史的开局或许改写——这桩假设，正是读五代末史时最耐人寻味的关节。

bio_parts_en.value: Chai Rong reigned barely six years, yet he was the hinge between what came before and after at the close of the Five Dynasties: he inherited the newly founded enterprise of his adoptive father Guo Wei, Taizu of Later Zhou, and opened the way to the unification completed under

Zhao Kuangyin. This page builds its chronology on the "Annals of Shizong" in the Zhou shu of the Old History of the Five Dynasties, supplemented by the "Zhou Basic Annals" in the New History of the Five Dynasties and the Zizhi Tongjian (all held in the local reference library).

In Xiande 1 Guo Wei died and Chai Rong succeeded, keeping the Xiande era name. When the allied armies of Northern Han and the Khitans pressed the border, he campaigned in person and defeated them at Gaoping; after the battle he purged and reorganized the palace army, establishing a new ruler's authority in a single stroke. His domestic policy was equally decisive: in Xiande 2 he restricted temples, reduced the clergy, and melted bronze Buddha statues for coin to fund finances and armament; across the Xiande years he further selected and trained the palace army and equalized land taxes, bringing state power back up.

In the south he campaigned against Southern Tang year after year, raising armies in Xiande 3 and maneuvering repeatedly in Huainan through Xiande 4 and 5, until in Xiande 5 Southern Tang ceded the lands north of the river and Zhou took fourteen prefectures, pushing the frontier to the north bank of the Yangzi, the very precursor of the passive position later faced by the line of

bio_parts_en.label: Li Yu, last ruler of Southern Tang

bio_parts_en.value:
. In Xiande 6 he turned to a northern expedition against the Khitans, recovered the Three Passes and prefectures of Guannan with his spearhead pointed toward Youzhou, but fell gravely ill in the field and had to turn back.

Back in Kaifeng he entrusted his young heir to Fan Zhi and others and died soon after; his son Zongxun succeeded as a child. The next year came the Chenqiao Mutiny, and Zhou yielded to Song; his unfinished ambition of unification was taken up and completed by the Song. Historians often dwell on his early death: had he been granted long years, the opening chapter of Song history might have been rewritten. That counterfactual is the most thought-provoking knot in reading the history of the late Five Dynasties.

emperors.summary: 陈桥兵变代周建宋，杯酒释兵权以强干弱枝，先南后北平定诸国的开国之君。
emperors.summary_en: The founding emperor who replaced the Zhou and founded the Song through the Chenqiao Mutiny, released his generals' military power over a cup of wine to strengthen the trunk and weaken the branches, and pacified the rival states south first and north later.

timeline.title: 陈桥兵变
timeline.summary: 兵变黄袍加身，代周建宋，定都开封。陈桥是否预谋为争议层。
timeline.summary_en: The mutiny draped him in the yellow robe; he replaced the Zhou, founded the Song, and fixed the capital at Kaifeng, though whether Chenqiao was premeditated remains disputed.

timeline.title: 定都开封
timeline.summary: 宋都汴京，五代积习上的新朝。
timeline.summary_en: The Song made Bianjing its capital, a new dynasty built on the accumulated habits of the Five Dynasties.

timeline.title: 杯酒释兵权
timeline.title_en: Dismissal over a Cup of Wine
timeline.summary: 以酒宴方式解除禁军宿将兵权，强干弱枝开端；细节有演绎。
timeline.summary_en: Over a wine banquet he stripped veteran palace-army generals of their commands, opening the path of strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches; the details have been embellished in later retellings.
